--- 帖子 #1 ---
Trading is part of my life and TDI indicator and APB are the main parts of my trading style. I appreciated lots of traders from Trading Made Simple thread where it made me become who I am today. As per title stated I use 30 minutes chart to enter and exit my fx trades ( I do check other time frames (M15 H1 H4) before taking my trades just to see any conflicts/facing S/R etc,. Sound straight forward doesn't it? No, why? Because things happen in between entry and exit that make it not so straight and that is still a learning curve to a lot of traders and myself I will post my trades here for sharing and discussing purposes. Please do not follow them without doing your due diligence. I take no responsibilities for any losses that may occur at your end. my favorite set ups are divergence and hidden divergence. Rules: TDI green crossed red off S/R, trade away from Daily Open Line (DOL), 200 EMA, and weekly S/R. I enter on M30 with these confirmation: - TDI cross/bounce - APB same color with my trade - @S/R - TL (trendline) breakout or special candle patterns (can be outside bar/inside bar/pull back candle,lower high/lower lows, higher high/higher lows, etc.) Note : I use Stochastic for extra confirmation and Awesome to see market momentum. Main focus is on price actions around support/resistant levels and get in a trade when TDI crosses forming divergence/hidden divergence. Locations are very important, and if you have divergence set up at good level, 99.99% you will have nice bag of greenies, but make sure you don't go short while TDI&gt;68, stoc&gt;75 (overbought= market too bullish ), nor go long while TDI&lt;32 (oversold = too bearish), stoc&lt;25. In addition with those conditions and with TDI cross and APB same color, it will be safer to go short when Stoc&lt;50, and long when stoc&gt;50. My trading time: Frankfurt Open(FO), London Open (LO), New York open (NY) English is not my first language so I will try to explain by showing it on my charts if needed. I will try to post my trades as early as possible after I entered them if I have time to do so. Managing trades is still my hardest part where I need to master it, where I need to master my emotion As I am a active trader I might not be available here all the time. I also might not have all answer to all queries, and the purposes of this thread is to share and discuss so please assist one another and important thing is be helpful and stay positive even when your account is not positive on the day, we all have positive and negative days, so deal with it in a appropriate manner by taking our own responsibilities and not blaming the market nor others. This is an advance system for those who knows the basis PA. If you are new to FX, please give yourself time to study the basis first on babypips then come back here to join us and learn more.Please go to paper clip on top right hand corner of this thread to download all indies I use. Happy trading! My current template (LKC TMS 2018.zip) added on 24th Feb 2018 worked to me but not to others, so on 13th Oct 2021 I replaced a template with a help from trader named Derek-205 for others to use. If any problem, please ask him or a tech person to help as I have no clue how to fix a tech problem. Cheers

--- 帖子 #60 ---
I will list my arguments about M30 time frame: I think that the higher trend is not adequately represented in the lowest, in the ratio of one to four. 4 H better "split" into eight parts. Just as the daily trend very well "split" on the hourly chart, the same 4 H chart a better look at the M30. So, for anyone who wants to trade using the 4 hour chart, it will be extremely useful to all information that he will find on this blog. In addition, the M30 - fine filter of the first noise from the crowd, at the beginning of each season. Wait for the next candle at H1 - too late, and the next M30 (after the start of the Session) - Just in time. And finally, the Dean Malone, the creator of almost all TMS based on, in his instructional videos, prefers this period. Clips with M 30 - more than any other frames. I wish this blog to become a true destination for acquiring knowledge for beginners. and for those of us who are a little more experienced - a place where we enjoy fellowship with each other, share experiences - free of any intrigue, and the dictatorship of ignorant selfish subjects recruiting newcomers into their "Skype rooms" - phenomenon which is observed on that, other blog "with the naked eye".

--- 帖子 #89 ---
your snap shot of GU is looking good on M30 H1 just that I don't like trading those pairs during Asian sessions. A good set up can be: - tdi crossed just above MBL for a long and just cross just below MBL for a short and away from those lines (200ma, DOL, weekly S/R) - TDI angle where you see green line heading down 5 o'clock (short) or 1 o'clock (long) and red line also heading to same direction as green - price make HH HL (long), LH LL (short) after divergence between price and TDI. I'd love to hear your thoughts and others too.

--- 帖子 #223 ---
Found this on the SynPro trading manual regarding expected profit targets for different time frames which may give an idea as to what one should realistically target/expect. Scalper Trades 1 - 5 minute charts. Uses 1-hour chart or less for market trend. Seeks 3 - 8 pips per trade. Active – Aggressive Trades 5 - 15 minute charts. Uses 4-hour chart or less for market trend. Seeks 5 - 15 pips per trade. Active – Conservative Trades 15 - 30 minute charts. Uses 4-hour chart for market trend. Seeks 20 - 40 pips per trade. Swing Trades 1 - 4 hour charts . Uses 4-hour chart for current trend and Daily chart for market trend. Seeks 40 - 100 pips per trade. Position Trades 4 hour – Daily charts . Uses 4-hour chart for entry &amp; exit, Daily chart for current trend, and Weekly chart for market trend. Seeks 100+ pips per trade.

What i really like about the d.o.t.s is that its very easy to use, and it finds the sl &amp; tp target. Personally i have no problem trading the tms, but i often make mistakes and expecting to much of the market, using this indicator, it finds the tp level for me. The indicator automatic plots the target, and that combined with a valid tdi cross, you often got a VERY strong trade. st=sell target bt=buy target ssl=sell stop loss bsl=buy stop loss Happy trading, and congratz with your biiiiiig bag of greens today :-)

Hi Erebus, No I didn't use any filters and I only tested LO. I have just been running a blind test placing pending orders in both directions closing half the order at tp1 and moving sl to be and letting the 2nd half of the order run to tp or sl. And then looking at the trades to see what happened. The results basically confirm the tms strategy , Trading away from DOL, weekly support/resistance, long above pac short below etc. I also found that the TDI from the higher TF filters out a lot of fake outs and gives a more accurate sense of direction. so far tp 1 got hit 81% tp2 73%, however tp 2 often gets smashed and the pips get cut short but you get very few losing trades if you moved to BE and take profit at target 1. Oh and quiet days are rubbish busy days good. I will post my results in a separate thread when I have more data. Hope that helps.

Sorry for those who PM me, since I run this thread and trading I found it s too much to also reply PM. Here one of PM I received which I am answering here so others might benefit and share their experiences. 1. Do you always trade away from the DOL? Is this a solid rule? I ask because like with GU, EU etc yesterday, there were big moves and you would have missed it as it was above the DOL? yes, most of the time I tried to trade away from it, if there s a signal and has space for PT I would take it. 2. I use SupDem on my charts, and sometimes when the market is in a small range SupDem creates both the blue and red bars very close together. As a rule, I dont like trading into these supply and demand zones, but how do you distinguish which are the false ones? I don't pay much attentions to that indie, I use weekly S/R, Daily High Low, DOL 3. I also added the MTF TDI to my charts, but I also see that sometimes the market makes big moves even when the MTF hasnt crossed? Do you just leave out these trades if ALL your rules have not passed your checks? MTF TDI is there for me to scale up/avoid trading overbought/oversold. You don't have to wait for it to cross, bending down/up to the same direction of your trades will help. TDI with right PA is the most important, other indies on my chart are treated as bonuses, if paying attentions to all indies on your chart and not PA you miss the principal.

One question that comes up a lot is about Risk:Reward... the thing is with TMS, it looks like the R:R is nuts cause Big E said to place your SL @ the previous pivot L or H. So you got to look @ the overall R:R [like per W1] and not on a trade by trade. Sounds a bit odd but like Big E said the SL is rarely hit cause when a trade starts to look bad [for whatever reason] you get out and focus on something else (just like Big E said). Last W1 my overall R:R was just over 1:4 - sweet spot

Upcoming Risk Event - Eurozone CPI Flash Estimate (10:00 am London time) Summary Figures are expected to come in roughly the same with last month providing a downside surprise of -0.6% against the forecast -0.5% don't expect these figures to improve until ECB QE starts taking effect, as such these data points are slightly irrelevant until we see the effects of QE. Any positive figures run contrary to the argument of a weakening EUR as such you're going to want to sell into any EUR rallies , so view any gains made by the currency as a good opportunity to get in and start selling it back, especially against the USD. Expected Market Reaction There is plenty of room for the EUR to fall further, you can continue to sell this currency on any rallies against stronger currencies like the USD and GBP. We expect any rallies on EUR/USD to be sold off, particularly if CPI continues to come out weaker, you want to look for good levels of resistance to sell EUR/USD.

Hi TMS 30M'ers, I have PMs asking about the chart indis I use - they are all info type indis ; 100pip handle lines - essential to know these IMO ( https://www.mql5.com/en/code/9197 ) Asian Session close / channel - typically knowing the range of the Asian and comparing to ADR will give idea of possible pips available ( http://www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php?t=239188 ) P4L Clock - excellent clock with ADR/range/vol etc ( http://www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php?t=109305 ) - also download his candle time indi (important for us in TMS) Hope this helps! --- 帖子 #883 ---
USD – ADP Non-Farm Employment Change This is a prelude to NFP it isn't the major event but gives us an indication as to what NFP might be like, the key to NFP is for it to be over 200k that is the psychological level that the market looks to. Figures are expected higher than previous and I believe that they will which will provide a reason for the USD to be supported going into next week, things could change throughout the week leading into the event but as it stands now we can expect these events to be positive for the USD. The Fed have said specifically that they are watching labour market data to which ends NFP is the primary measure of labour market health and this along with average earnings is one of the data points which they are basing their decision on whether to hike or not. If it continues to come out positive as it has over the last few months there are even less reasons for the Fed to delay. The other thing that has been positive for the USD recently was core CPI, the headline figure lacked momentum but the core which removes oil prices was very healthy, ticked higher than expected and was supportive of our USD bias going into the week. CAD – BOC Rate Statement &amp; Overnight Rate Decision This data point is important as the market is interested in whether the BoC will cut or hold, the general consensus was that they would cut until last Tuesday when Poloz spoke. Everyone was expecting Poloz to be dovish which he was but he made one comment that spooked the market and made them doubt whether the BoC would cut rates further, he said that after the first rate cut the BoC are now prepared to take a step back and observe what impact that rate cut has had, they don’t feel any pressure to cut further until they've seen the impact of the cut. Of course many traders interpreted this as they are not going on the 4th which makes sense but the one caveat I would add to that is that the BoC don’t provide forward guidance because of this indecision I will not be trading going into this event.

--- 帖子 #1089 ---
Thanks Likica. I'm doing really well in oil. To be honest it was studying your charts that got me into it. It's difficult to explain in words because I follow it and have a feel for it. I set up a pending order using an ea with an entry at a break of a certain point. In this case the pivot line. I also use trend lines, weekly highs and lows. I don't make the trade live yet I just wait for a tdi cross and 3 red/green in the matrix then I click the live button. I try and wait for the market to come to me then jump on. I know pending orders aren't everyone's cup of tea. But my success has massively improved since I learnt how to use them. takes all of the emotion out of it and forces me to plan my entry and exit. Hope I explained it well.

Hi Jim, You might want to try take profit at ATR, or at S/R or when opposite apb appear (check my trade snapshots for my style if you like or Griffinssoul's style) or move your SL and PT as the trade progress like some other super traders here (Omonisha, RedcloudXlll,...), who have done more than +100 pips per trade. Hi Mario, I guess you were just asking as you saw it look handy. From my experience, any TDI and APB can do the job perfectly, addition features can get you distracted and forget about price actions. I saw lots of traders (newbies) jumped in a trade when seeing TDI crossed by only looking at arrows appeared and did not pay attentions to size of apb (big/small, long wicks small body, etc..) , or if price was stepping up or down, nor any support/resistance nearby... Hi Mokuro, You can only use what you have and work around that, and if NY is the only time you can trade then do your research and stick to one or 2 pairs that have decent move around that session and have realistic profit targets for your trades, don't get too intimidated about us who can trade LO. Good luck!

--- 帖子 #1770 ---
Hi Vay, if you think you are still newbie, pick 1 pair only and study its movement until you are confident. Gj has nice and fast move normally around LO and during NY too. I personally don't like GU but took it a few times with good PA for small PT. Highest ADR can be a good thing to pick, don't take all of 3 or 6 as they don't always go in the same direction. I switch between charts (M15 M30 H1 H4), if you see a signal formed in M30 or H1, it is ok to switch to M15 to enter ( I did it sometimes after news), specially with G pairs. Master you PA readin skill to be selective with TDI signals as there are so many signals during the day. Just sharing these 2 shorts I saw TDI confirming on M30, didn't want to waste pips so I switched charts to M15 and entered from the break out, bagged 60 green each while they still moved further down. I don't normally enter from M15 by itself if no confirmation on M30 or H1, and avoid trade M30 into 200ema, DOL, weekly S/R. If there s still space to move between price and 200ema to feed your PT, why not? Hope my sharing makes sense.

I wanted to get this group's opinion. Due to lack of free time, I cant trade the lower time frames. I noticed that the daily charts offer very good accuracy rate if one does not enter carelessly. I use stochastic over bought and over sold area and match it with the TDI angle to find relative peak and trough. If trades are not entered carefully, the price can move against me for 100-200 pips before getting into the green territory. But as you can see, stochastic is very helpful in making my trade decisions. The Price point matched up with every stochastic low eventually gets to a higher stochastic level with a higher price; and vice versa. I know this thread trade the 30 minute chart but I think the daily could be a big help to ensure you are trading with the next targeted price direction. Anything the seasoned traders can provide some guidance on a better way to enter, I would appreciate very much. What do you do to gauge how much the pair might move? For example, take the second circle and compare that to the third circle. Other than the slope of the TDI, is there another way? The truth is, it would be very difficult for anyone to make money for buying from the signal (circle 3 from left to right) although it did eventually end up higher 17 days later. PS, I know some thread doesnt like it when others use additional indicators on their chart, if that is an issue just let me know. Thanks.

Hi Aw, Welcome to M30. As per GS said, we are 'young' and active on M30. I can share a bit of my 'young' experience as follows: - I agree with you that when stoc with TDI used it seem to help, specially if it just moved out of overbought/oversold (80/20 levels) and TDI moved out of 68/32 levels regardless time frame. - I agree with you trading from D1 is less complicated than lower TF, however, for me it s very hard to handle when seeing my trades retraced 50pips unless I had very small vol placed - I would try to avoid choppy and retraced areas where both stoc &amp; TDI turned down around oversold ( no sells), and where stoc and TDI turned up around O/bought ( no buys) I would look at both TDI and stock when TDI signal appeared and TDI and stoc look like what I marked X on the chart (they both turned down around oversold) I would wait as it had no room to move down so it had to move up before it move down again. - I would look at APB size and its form/shape (not too small (not qualified as confirmed APB) not too large( will retrace)) to qualify our entries as well as per Big E rule is to enter on 1st APB, if 1st APB too small 2nd apb is acceptable. - PT can be: 1st PT: ATR (7) X 1 , 2nd PT = ATF (7) X 1.5, 3rd ATR(7) X 2. For counter trend, I would take PT = ATR(7) X 1 only. - SL should be 10pips away from 2nd last APBs. * Don't worry about adding indicators if it helps you. For me I have AO on my chart to quickly see what momentum the market is at the time I want to place trade and it s quick to see if any divergence forming.... * For others they might not need any more than TDI and levels S/R like weekly/EMAs,.... By the way, AU might be choppy/dive a bit more before it head up from where it is currently sitting as stock is below 20 and TDI has not crossed yet. I noticed that divergence forming but not confirmed yet....If you jumped in at closed of last red APB (if you entered on H4 TDI crossed), it has already moved +100 in your favour, you should expect a retrace before it moves up again.... IMO.

--- 帖子 #2409 ---
thanks for sharing ur trades both winners and losers which is good for us to learn. I noticed your GCAD loser was a counter trend and entered on M15, which a habit that lots of us did including myself when seeing divergence. The smaller TF we trade, the harder it get right since we have to look at lots of things such as levels, TDI of next HTF to see if it s not at o/b or o/s areas, recent PA to see if buyers or seller strong... When price was below 10ma 50ma 200ma I would only think of selling. Counter trend is the hardest thing to do IMO whether divergence or at s/r . That's why I rarely go with M15 unless I have backkup from H1 M30 and decide to take small PT . If one like to take trades on M15, I would suggest you find your edge such as only take TDI trades when price is below/above all 3 emas and reverse (10ema, 50ema 200ema) and having double tops/bottoms or having lower high.... to be safe ( I trade oil/gold on M15 sometimes entered on M5 during fast/volitile move hrs, but I tell u it's not easy). Of course there are always some winners not following rules but would we want to sit there and be nervous while breaking rules ? The easy way is to find divergence/hidden divergence on small TF but with trend but avoid trade into s/r.... Here are 2 examples on GCAD M15 (during London hrs): - divergence where price broke all 3 EMA and reversed (bounced 3 times and created lower high then headed down again) - divergence counter trend facing 200ema (Longman's trade that failed) and hidden divergence with trend to show that it's safer to go with trend If you don't have any EMA on your chart beside 200EMA, that's ok if you are good at reading PA (like driving without GPS unless you know your way ). If you don't even have 200EMA on, I bet you have to switch to a few charts to identify trend and S/R before entering your trades.... By the way, I m not an expert on m15 so I would like to hear from others who have more experience on M15 to share for us to learn too.

--- 帖子 #2495 ---
Hi Ken, Thanks for your compliment. I have my bad and good too. what I found is when I follow my rules and not trying too hard to break them (I still do sometimes ), I do not feel stressed whether the trades turned out red or green. Asian session normally have small move and if you are aware of it, set your PT realistic to bag and run if you happen to spot a nice looking signal ( I usually spot 1 per day) I dont really like leaving my trades from Asian to FO/LO unless I have good reasons or unable to monitor them. Yeah, there are lots of news scheduled around LO and best to let it cool down at least 15 min before entering a trade if there s a signal confirmed or PA still valid with support from fundie (you would say most of news are BS ). If you looked at my GU short I entered around 2pm my time which was opened until after LO to have PT filled (I posted yesterday), u would say I must have had balls to stay in as it moved -25 from my entry. I was watching where that FO/LO apb moved and closed and it actually closed below my DOL so I stayed in. I saw lots of traders entering right at LO and price immediately moved -20 pips or more against them and they jumped out. Try to avoid that fake move by not entering at open of new hour, you still have chance to enter after 15min/30min later....study PA very important to me as I need reason to enter and stay with my trade until current candle completed. You can have 10EMA on your chart to see if price close below or above it to stick with your trade, you can see TDI hooked/crossed but it could move back up/down, while PA is more accurate IMO. I believe experienced/successful traders pay attentions to PA and occassionally glance at indies but not the other way around. It better if you post snapshot of your chart with your trades here so you will learn (not to repeat those mistakes) and so will we. Happy trading and green day to all. L Thanks J. I m very lucky to have chance to learn and share to/from others

--- 帖子 #3371 ---
I dont use a fixed number os pips, I use a fixed % of my equity and put the SL behind the last swing or cross PA example: Attached Image USDCAD today, SL behind the PA and last swing, 25 pip SL and 25 pip TP 1:1 R:R, It could be 30, the TP would be 30 either But i'm not sure if this is the best aproach, neither i'm sure about the R:R ratio

--- 帖子 #3372 ---
Makuro,, I always set a 50 pip emergency stop but then monitor the trade as it goes. When the trade is up 25 pips I move my stop to break even then its a free trade with no pressure. If the apb has a shadow wick or tdi turns and things turn against me I like to get out before I lose full 50 pips. You need to check your pac as well and if apb closes above or below the 5 ma against me , then im out the trade. Now if trade moves in my direction I dont close untll I see any of the above happening. Just observe price action at resistance levels, if there are no wicks and no kink in tdi and price still outside the pac do not close the trade. By doing this your return will over time be higher than your losses and you will find you get a lot of 2 -1 and even 3 -1. Study big OM posts to see how this is done.

--- 帖子 #3446 ---
Here is my GA M30 chart with PAC (for some who will find its benefit to have it on to avoid entering on small bodied APBs ) with a few basic rules: - Go long when APB closed above PAC, - go short when ABPs closed below PAC - avoid trade into S/R (look left to see) - avoid trade into 200MA &amp; DOL - take profit/exit when price creates double tops/ bottoms or an opposite APB. If you focus on 1 chart like M30 for long enough, you will notice its patterns. I was lucky to be advised by one of senior trader when I was very new to trading, he told me to play around with my chart, study it carefully by looking left to see if recent candles are red or green, big or small, manually draw lines/ trend lines, etc. to really feel the move... ) I found that on some occasions (only some where price bounced off strong S/R) we can enter early on breakout (white trendline) of a series of inside bars/small APBs (don't have to wait until APBs closed). Don't get hooked into a trap where a series of same color of small APBs then sudden one big and same color apb formed... in this case look and wait to go opposite. Best entries (from Big'E TMS rules still apply to any TF) is entering on 1st or 2nd APB, if TDI confirmed on 3rd APB, leave it, wait for next set up. And my best entries are when red green TDI cross just above ( for buy)/below (for sell)yellow line (marked as grey rectangles) of course with decent body APB (small tiny apbs won't be qualified). Pls share your thoughts. Thank you.

--- 帖子 #3478 ---
Hi M, The indie named 'ADR_V2' from paper clip. I usually use adr for pair selection if I have to pick one to trade, or scanning if there s a big move happened from recent session to tell me to look for reversal. Frankly, I only pay attention to S/R to take PT. I welcome everyone everything that helps that person to make their trade turn out good, but for me I m not that keen on additional indies. Pay attentions to price, tdi, and for me I need Awesome Osc as I m still not really good at reading PA without AO for additional filter to take counter trend and continuations. I m an artistic type and enjoying playing with indies, but for serious decision, I base on my core (look at price to see how ready my surrounding is and TDI to get in). For Profit taking, I don't need to bag the whole move, leave some for others . IMO, you r on the right track to use last swing for PT/SL unless you monitor your trades and things happened that made you exit your trade earlier such as news, market running out of steam, or blah blar... As long as your SL smaller than PT, you should end your month in green ( note that don't let market take u out, SL is there to protect u from unforseen circumstance). I m having morning (Melbourne time) coffee the road right now (my lovely niece's birthday today, need to get something for special dinner ), When I have time, I will talk more about GA EA shorts that many traders took and some ended with a loss during LO yesterday (Mon 18th) I won't be avail for FO LO today (Tue 19th). --- 帖子 #3642 ---
start thinking like a 'market maker'... say you want to move the market higher but you need the funds to do so - how can you achieve this goal? well if the chart says PA should be breaking high you slam it short - but it may be that that itself sets off a chain reaction and shorts the market - no one can dictate PA (IMO) absolutely that is why probability is the closest thing you can have... set your R:R b/w 1:1 and 1:2 (or better) and in the long run you should be ok

--- 帖子 #3643 ---
If I'm thinking like a market maker, and I want to move the market higher, I need to push the price DOWN to create the orders / liquidity that I need to buy into. I don't believe that market makers set off accidental chain reactions. They know exactly where they want price to go and will take it in that direction.

--- 帖子 #3695 ---
I'd double L on the comments...said it all. If you look left, there's consolidation since end of NY yesterday, with price bouncing off 20-30 pips on either side of the DOL. Those chops will eat your pips and your nerves as well. Wait for clear PA - breakouts from the consolidation areas, good sized APB candles, clear trends, divergences, BRN's, whatever it is you choose to follow... and ONLY THEN look down at your oscillator TDI - if it confirms what you see. If you watch every swing during the H1 or M30 candle, it can go20-30 pips in either direction, you'll go crazy - for no reason at all. I did it for weeks and it is not fun at all. It's horrible. And there's no logical justification of doing it (other than self whipping).

--- 帖子 #3697 ---
had a few PMs about PTs and MoneyM - short answers is i have been going around in circles on this problem... if PA is brutal (for your style of trading) and your TPs are not getting hit you will lose - simple answer is to not trade or change your style (move up a TF for example) on MM all senior traders, Phx62, LW, SJ, Emm, TSS, etc all have simple approaches with partial target structures... complicating this does not seem to help at all and in fact may do the complete opposite. The best PTs traders i have seen on ff are my buddies - OS on the HTFs and LK on the LTFs my current setup is based on five parts of one (whole) trade that way i can weight things differently as i need - for example if i think PA will reverse soon i will go in with a 4/5 PTs set to say 50pips and let the last ride or if i feel more confident fan out 3/5 PTs as 50/60/70 then see what happens with the last two - maybe set one to 90 then the next to the next RN etc i should add that i have seen no evidence that taking PTs over just one TP is of any benefit - in fact some senior traders here on ff say there is no benefit profit wise - but for me it is of gr8 benefit psychologically

TSS posted some analysis on EJ http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...41#post8310241 have a read if you want to trade ABCD patterns OS has posted some PA analysis on EA http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...89#post8310289 - i highly recommend learning the analysis of these traders Here is my W1 review of EJ @ the LO and how to use the H4 [with a Lastingwell edge].... first step is to note the angle of the H4... we are looking for alignment/agreement for the M30 TDI cross [dotted vertical lines are LO+1 - green/orange/red circles are buy/no trade/sell] first chart Then assess the situation @ the M30... i have only done the first one but you can have a look your self (2nd chart)... +40+230+65+60pips (conservative estimate - would have bagged +150pips (single trades) and one BE - Wed no trade - H4 flat green line - this could have still been traded but just not @ LO) - you should keep in mind this is by no means a backtest - proper backtests are faced with many technical problems and require durations greater than 3 MNs - side note - there is a further problem here cause of candle close which is why merrygold suggested making a histogram type indi but i am still pondering that one... side note 2 - Lastingwell uses the H4 much more effectively than this but i only trade LO

--- 帖子 #3991 ---
Hi Shay, I know you were asking GS but while I m here I drop you a hint ( I mentioned it a few times), pay attentions to levels and APBs and go from there...while TDI can be a cross or a bounce or even a bend/curve as lots of time you wait for a good angle and end up entering after a big APB and suffering a big retrace before seeing it heading to your trade direction. Here is how I trade: - get ready when we see price is parking around S/R (200MA/50MA, Wkly S/R, Fibs, prev swing low/high....etc.) and see if it is above or below 200MA to go long or short. - and watch how price reacting from those levels (pin bars or inside/outside bars or divergence,...) - then look at TDI and count APB to see if it is the right moment to enter... It might sound conflict to other traders who told you to look at TDI first, as for those seniors they can do either ways and won't miss any step. However, I found that lots of traders first looked at TDI and got excited when there was a TDI cross and jumped in before even looked at PA and S/R , then next few minute got stopped out. It's up to you to adjust to fit your trading style. Have a good and greener week to all

--- 帖子 #3993 ---
"so much anxiety that I mostly close my trades prematurely." - try decreasing your risk to a manageable level then increase with confidence "scaling out and/or adding to running positions. " - scaling out is gr8 for psychology - adding to position is not - not a good idea and here is why - say you have a winning trade @40pips and you have set to BE - then you add another position and the trade goes against you - you have gone from a free trade to a losing one - this will impact your psychology more than just a straight loss [building your account by compounding is totally different to building a trade - compounding is a very powerful thing for your account] I base my PT on all the typical PA - candle size, S&amp;R, ADR, etc still working on this part and probably will be for a long time... oh, and the most important thing R:R !!!

Here is one of PM I received asking me the followings and most of them I already mentioned in the past. I will answer them here again for others who missed my prev posts might find them useful. Could you please tell me some about your money management plan? 1. How many lots do you open for each trade? I mean do you multi open or open one position and close it all at the target? I use single entries but sometimes I enter with multi entries when price pull back at strong S/R 2. What is your take profit for each trade. İf any. I usually aim PT = 50 but change it as the trade in good progress 3. What is your daily, weekly target and what is the usual result? weekly target: 1000 green pips 4. Do you only trade 30 min? yes it s my main TF but I have H1 up as well, checking M15 during fast moving time (NY/UScash) and when seeing H1 price @ strong S/R 5. Which currencies do you trade? I like GA GJ EA EJ EN, occassionally take GN GU EU (I m not good with pairs like AU NU) 6. What is your stop loss? How much do you risk for each trade? pre SL = 50 but change as trade in progress or exit early if PA change. Cutting my loss is what I normally do if I monitor my trades, I recommend not to let SL get hit if seeing things not working. R: R 1:1. Pls note that I still have lots to learn from you too. Pls share your experience for all to learn. Happy pipping

--- 帖子 #4301 ---
The riddle of DOL... when you use a rule like ours "trade away from the DOL" what it really does is filter out certain types of D1 candles @ the LO - mainly indecision candles like dojis, spinning tops, etc - and related trades... in this first chart of EU D1 we can pick out a variety of different types of candles that make up the bullish move (5-wave impulse move)

--- 帖子 #4302 ---
...lets have a closer look @ the green box... as a candle stick this has no (or small) lower wick (half marubosu) so we caught the LO power of the move north... a perfectly timed trade TMS M30 [purple line is DOL]

--- 帖子 #4303 ---
...but wat we are filtering out is trades like this one... the blue box... a nice +30pips over the asian session but then we move into the DOL going back - which as it turns out has a nice TDI cross - then near the LO we had to be very careful not to get trapped short ...the idea is that it is less likely to encounter this scenario than the first (above) or similar... notice 1 - that the most profitable trade of the D1 went against the rule notice 2 - the rule alone can not save you from being trapped or a bad trade in general notice 3 - the uptrend is made up of a variety of different candles ...since some of the smartest and most experienced traders on ff are debating this point http://www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php?t=533279 i will leave this with you and hope that it has helped

--- 帖子 #4412 ---
hey SuperBlue - here is some info regarding the difference b/w HA, APB, HA Smoothed, APB Smoothed etc, as I was confused about this (as were other traders - so I hope this is of some benefit ). This was from one of my early posts when i was starting out Dean Malone modified the definition of HA as he reasoned they were developed for non-fx trading and not as suitable for fx. So, he changed the way the HA_Close was found. If you have a look @ the way HA candles are found, HA_Close = (Open + High + Low + Close) / 4 HA_Open = (HA_Open [previous candle] + HA_Close [previous candle]) / 2 HA_High = Max (High, HA_Open, HA_Close) HA_Low = Min (Low, HA_Open, HA_Close), changing the way HA_Close is found changes (almost) everything else. The Open, High, Low, Close is just the normal OHLC. I dont know what the change to this is exactly but you could make 10Billion ones no doubt [probably something simple]. The smoothed version(s) simply take values from the average (MA's) values from the OHLC values to use instead of just the hard values, (OHLC themselves). The advantages of APB are; 1. follows current Close better 2. reduce potential extreme HA_Low/High values - I take this to mean when, for e.g., HA_Open is higher than High etc 3. reduction in noise It is the first point that seems most advantageous to TMS'ers as we heavily rely on the candle close.

Every trader must develop their own trading plan and what works for them. Learning to trade mechanically (with little emotion over wins or losses), learning money management and learning to evaluate each trade based on its merits (not overtrading) are all key ingredients of a successful trading plan." - Phx62

Hi all. I noticed that having been posting a few of my trade charts here the last few weeks that I haven't introduced myself to the group. I would like to thank Likica (And others) for their huge efforts and contributions to this thread and the sharing of ideas. My trading methodology for the last few years uses daily fibo pivots and round numbers and 200ema as target S/Rs. My 'system' evolved out of the stoch tape genesis trading 5/15m method (if any FF members here know of RJ and have seen/studied this particular system, you will know of its simplicity). I then later added TMS replacing HA with Dean Malones APB/ price channel. My results have been excellent however I feel I by closing my trades at stages still using round numbers and daily pivots (rather than straight reversal candle) that I'm leaving pips 'on the table' this is something I've had to live with as part of trading. --- 帖子 #4729 ---
Hi Binary, I suppose and I'll leave others to add to this but I would suggest that which every time frame you decide to trade; that you should check the higher timeframes... so if trading 5m, then 15m and 30m.... 15m, check 30m or 1h... if 1h, then 4h and D1 etc. This will help you assess the overall trend and avoid taking false/contradicting signals on your chosen time frame if going against the trend in higher timeframe. But cant stress enough that whichever time frame you decide you should be looking at the Daily charts, to gauge market sentiment and overall trend. Personally I trade intraday and use both the 15m and 30m frames and consult the D1, however its personal experience and faith; so its whatever is comfortable and unique to every trader. Good luck with you trading

--- 帖子 #4737 ---
Excellent advice SB . I'd to make it a bit more details about my purpose of looking at higher time frames H4 H1 are to know my environment for the day. 1st thing I look on M30 is to find where my 200EMA is, then looking at the below on all H4 H1 M30 (if any): - support or resistant nearby?, - double tops/double bottoms?, - divergence/ hidden divergence? - inside bar, pin bar? Zoom in zoom out all charts ( H4 H1 M30) to see...learn to know your market before getting in any trade. Once you are in it, you tend to see only your feeling (excited/stressed) M30 is where I get in when TDI gives signals I usually think of trading like driving....Before going anywhere, we need to look for address and direction. During driving we do look left and right, rear and ahead, we don't just go/turn when green light on but watch out if condition is safe to do so...if we did not, we could end up hurting ourself even many times we follow rules....blah blah blah... It only you can give yourself experience and confidence by practise,practise and practise... For entering a trade, I need 4 conditions: - TDI cross/turn - Support/ resistant - apb size (not small) - price actions (divergence/hidden divergence or double tops/bottoms, trendline breakout, high high higher low or lower high lower low...) For exit a trade, either one of these appear: - S/R - opposite APB -TDI cross/ turn back During big vol time like FO LO NY price moves fast and can give you fault signals to get out (apb turning to opp color), breath and think of the reasons you are in the trade to stay. If you get in with an invalid PA just because TDI cross and that's it or just because APB turns to the color of your trade without any S/R or what I mentioned above to support your trade, you then get nervous and get out as you have nothing else to hold on to. I hope what I shared and experienced could help some of you to get to next levels. Green pips and happy trading! L

i am so grateful for your contributions here OS - thnx heaps buddy !!! gr8 question dennis4u15 - put that line of your M30 chart - looks gr8 doesnt it - now dial up to H1 - its just crossing looks ok - now dial up to H4 - as you can see there is no H4 bend up and the Angleator was showing a retrace not a reversal - GCad and GA did reverse as supported by the Angleator signal - the other G's didnt and GN looked the best - i could have made 200pips on this trade remember pips themselves have no generic $[base] value - they were introduced as a unit so countries could trade easily converting etc - you need this calculators http://fxtrade.oanda.com/analysis/profit-calculator/ examples - ( http://fxtrade.oanda.com/learn/intro...nventions/pips ) Determine the number of CAD each pip represents by multiplying the amount of the trade by 1 pip as follows: 300,000 x 0.0001 = 30 CAD per pip Divide the number of CAD per pip by the closing exchange rate to arrive at the number of USD per pip: 30 1.0568 = 28.39 USD per pip Multiply the number of pips gained, by the value of each pip in USD to arrive at the total loss / profit for the trade: 20 x 28.39 = $567.80 USD profit

--- 帖子 #4840 ---
Thanks for the shout-out GS! Much appreciated, Can't echo your comments enough... the Phx62 PDF's are worth more than any $500 Ebook or $2,500 trading course that I've ever come across. My advice for anyone struggling on TMS intra-day trading would be to study these PDF's in great depth, and keep going over them them until you're up to speed with all the patterns and techniques covered. Similarly, if your looking for LTF's (M5 to M30) study charts and live trades posted by LK and GS. For HTF's (H4) OS and Emmanuel have some excellent material. Once you've studied the material, I'd say it's best to pick and follow 1 or 2 pairs for a while. You'll see many of the senior traders like LK, GS, OS etc. successfully trade many pairs but its best to keep things as simple as possible whilst learning. The less pairs you follow, the quicker and easier the learning IMO. Remember &lt;5% make it... give yourself the best chance possible. Secondly, post charts... there is a great community, both in here, and in the "Trading Made Simple" thread. We are lucky to have some extremely experienced and successful traders to trade alongside. As long as you are seen to be making an effort, and not asking questions that have been answered countless times already, all of the members I have come across, are happy to offer their advice and help out where they can. As GS said, this learning never stops...

--- 帖子 #5068 ---
ADR is the average daily range, so basically how much the pair moves in the day. The higher the number, the more it has moved, and therefore your profit/losses will be higher. The lower the number, the less the pair moves, and your profits/losses will be lower. Does that make sense?

--- 帖子 #5370 ---
Shadow, you are correct. Here's the instructions for how to set the TDI on your cell phone for those who want to double check their settings, or for those who want to add it for the first time. I keep a copy of these instructions in a folder on my desktop. ================= How to replicate the TDI using the standard RSI indicator. The Traders Dynamic Index aka TDI is actually 3 moving averages of the RSi data. The default parameters are: the TDI Price Line PL green line is a SMA(2) of the RSI(period 13, Close Price). Then the TDI Trade Signal Line red line is a SMA(7) of the PL green line. The TDI Market Base Line MBL yellow line is a SMA 34 period of the PL green line. You can replicate these using the platform standard RSI indicator: Steps: 1. Create RSI in a new window. Set the parameters to Period 13 and use the Close Price, and set the color to None, this will not show the RSI line. 2. Select and drag the Moving Average indicator into the sub-window as the RSI. Set the MA period to 2, Simple, Close, color = Green, and the most important last parameter is to, Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. 3. Select and drag the Moving Average indicator into the same sub-window as the RSI. Set the MA period to 7, Simple, Close, color = Red, and the most important last parameter is to, Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. 4. Select and drag the Moving Average indicator into the same sub-window as the RSI. Set the MA period to 34, Simple, Close, color = Yellow, and the most important last parameter is to, Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. Note: all three settings must be Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. The above setup should now show the TDI replicated with these default parameters: RSI_Period = 13 RSI_Price = 0 RSI_Price_Line = 2 RSI_Price_Type = 0 Trade_Signal_Line = 7 Trade_Signal_Type = 0 Market Base Line = 34 Market Base Line Type =0

--- 帖子 #5495 ---
Hi Mary4x, If you decide to trade using TDI indicator and price actions, any time frames and any pairs will works. In case you are new (from your profile you are not), concentrate to one pair and study the move of the session you are available to trade first. Let say you are only available during UScah session (9.30am est -4pm est) and choose EU/GU because its spread is cheap, put M30, h1, h4 charts up (if you want to enter trade on M30), find your edge such as only trade off S/R and divergence with TDI crosses... Do not enter a trade when TDI at overbought area (&gt;68) or at oversold area (&lt;32) even if TDI crosses until it moves out of those areas. We can give you lots of advice when to enter/exit, but I found that many traders including myself only studying old chars and practise and practise can give us confidence. Good luck.

--- 帖子 #5571 ---
The first mistake often made by China pessimists is to think that the market crash presages an economic collapse. That is most unlikely. True, the stock market is down by a third in a few weeks, but it has fallen back only to March levels; it is still up by 75% in a year . Lost in the drama is the fact that the stock market still plays a small role in China . The free-float value of Chinese markets the amount available for trading just about a third of GDP, compared with more than 100% in developed economies. Natural contraction in markets after thousands bought shares on borrowed money (margin trading ) To me its irrelevant http://www.economist.com/news/leader...china-embraces

--- 帖子 #5636 ---
Beautiful curve!Remember even simple cross over is profitable provided you don't let losses get out of control. My motto is learn to love taking a loss and winners will pile up. This is not directed to you but general.If you have anxiety of taking a 20 loss but let that become 250 loss then forced to take the loss is classic psychology malfunction. Trading is opposite of what we were taught since kids.We are taught always try to win try hard etc.Well in Trading opposite is true by allowing small losses to occur you open yourself bigger profits to rip. This is the hardest part in trading of which only few master.This part is crucial.Its not about systems or indicators.Its about humility to admit to yourself you made a error and close that error as soon as possible. Think of it another way every trade is basically a guesswork and best guesses overtime build equity. Richard Donchian whom I consider greatest trader ever lived started late in life in his 60's by 70 he was multimillionaire.He was the father of trend trading which inspired turtle trading. He was only 30% correct but still made millions.I don't care about % of wins what's important is size of the losses vs profits.

Hi Shay In my understanding (others feel free to correct) Angleleator is quick way to see where PA is in multiple time zones Black means flat sideway Best Trades for me is when at least 3 TF is red or green .Since most times I don't hold on to trades too long having daily opposite should not deter you from taking the trades since within a day they are lot of corrections that takes place. To me its quick visual guide and I love it. Angle position to me is irrelevant as long as there is cross and PA is going my direction. Some I read prefer 12 5 6 7 11 o'clock as strong moves and 234-8910 weaker.While this is generally true I don't particularly care myself about that as long as PA is moving my way and TDI cross is within tradeable zone.

You must establish your cutting point There is no such a thing as Zero loss trading.

Just sharing few thoughts since its Friday. On tRading This is tough endeavor only few survive FF is full of BS explorers people posting 1200% return a week and down 75% overall.Posting 800% return on 200 account is peanuts.Does not impress me nor should it impress you.What this mean the guy is over trading to a tilt and with 100 200 account blowing it away does not seem that damaging.In real world with real accounts people don't risk 75% on a single trade. If you got this attitude which is gamblers attitude just simply avoid this thread please. Realistically I shoot 10% monthly and more or less that's my goal.Making 10% a month in 36months is staggering purse. What this means every trade should be looked upon meticulously not lets shoot and see if it hits. We want to take only trades that confirm this thread's rules! Success is measured not by 2,3,4,5 trades but 20+ This is important because often people go from system to system and after losing few become endless gypsies searching for wholly grail. Stick with one method and master it. Things that are important 1.If wrong take the loss (there is certain degree of randomness in the market and there is no way you will be correct all the time.Richard Donchian was only correct 30% but he made millions by simply closing losses early and letting profits run) 2.Take reasonable TP but if you are in strong trend in good positions let it run 3.Market is king and your ego is your enemy .Submit to her don't fight the market 4.BE patient and let the trades come to you 5Check your greed meter! Biggest losses are result of greed not taking the small loss early and your ego convincing you know better then the market.You are just a tiny speck in the ocean.Always check your ego. Be humble give and receive. That's it for now. Enjoy the weekend

Not from the TDI indie, but from another RSI that I set up almost like the TDI itself. Don't need it to be 100% accurate - I'll look myself at that, but to indicate general area, whether ob or os...is enough. Also when price reaches a certain level, I get an e-mail from the Price Alert indie which draws the lines on the chart. Very helpful. Then I simply open the mobile platform (very basic) to check and decide if to enter. No more waiting time for me. Setting these alerts take 5 min daily, if they've been hit the previous day. Hi GS Great results! Looking at your chart you were progressively adding to losing positions from 9662 to 9630 If you intentionally were scaling like I do always then its fine but if you were just trying to recover by adding more and more same amount going far behind your intended lot traded then that's not so good.I believe you know what you are doing and you were scaling in.Danger of this instead of losing 20pips you end up forcefully closing -250pips. Just want to warn the lurkers and newbies this way to trade is not something you want to make habit of because you need serious screen time before adding to losing positions. Regards

--- 帖子 #6033 ---
Hi Claudio Your response to live trading is typical.Everyone goes through and for some pressure is too much to handle. There is a solution=Experience The way to overcome being nervous about money is to lower the lot traded as small as possible.Yes you won't make money with tiny lots but you won't lose a lot either.Goal for every beginner is to survive 1st 2years without blowing too many accounts.I am afraid there is no shortcut on screen time.No substitute. Demo trading only teaches technically how to make money and almost all who demo make easy money but obviously they can't replicate that with real money. Few pointers.Practice solid good healthy habits and opposite at your stage is detrimental.Changing a bad habit is much harder, its like playing piano with wrong fingering and later told you must correct.Well wrong fingering is now a muscle memory in your brain and will take serious mental effort to overcome but learning correct fingering from start is much more easier. .1 Develop a system or follow one like on this thread 2.Trades taken only based on this system 3.Stop loss is placed at the same time as the trade and not moved later 4 Practice patience let the trade come to you don't force it. 5.Keep a detail log why you took the trade win or lose specially on losses.Identify the mistake if not sure ask. Above covers in my opinion what you need but some reading is required 1. Trading in the Zone by Mark Douglas 2. Super Trader Make Consistent Profits in Good and Bad Markets by Van Tharp These 2 are enough to keep you busy next 12months.They are not easy books to read and practice but in my opinion what's easy in real world often have no merit. Regards

New Zealand co-operative group Fonterras dairy prices plummet Fonterra will pay farmers NZ$3.85 (2.32) per kilogram of milk solids in the season ending May 31st, 2016, it said yesterday. Dairy prices slumped to a 12-year low at this weeks GlobalDairyTrade auction amid a global glut, threatening to curb economic growth in a nation that relies on dairy for a quarter of its export earnings. Todays announcement implies NZ$3.3 billion less revenue than normal for Fonterras suppliers, said Michael Gordon , senior economist at Westpac Banking in Auckland . Prices are unsustainably low and we are seeing them beginning to impact production levels globally, chairman John Wilson said in the statement. 6640 is of interest to me.618 of recent swing

Thanks Forest for paying attention.Not posting for self glory but trying to make others think outside the box.Reason I like this system because its based on 30min chart.Most often moves are counter to main trend on 30min so in essence lots of trades taken on this system are against the main trend. Trend trading requires bigger account and wider stops because retacement can be big.For example on UC over 100pips and once it does come down 100pips 29.90 say your long entry was 3175 and now you are in significant DD and you don't know if current retrace is continuation of larger trend up or new trend reversing.This is the part new traders get killed trading trends.What they thought was still main trend going up most often is already trend going opposite.If you are trend trader be prepared to have as much as 15-20% DD or take regular losses and to me its not worth the risk. Hope this is not overwhelming.It takes some trading experience (3+years) to recognize when trend runs out of steam.Its something hard to explain. regards

--- 帖子 #6719 ---
Usually the candles foreshadow the exhaustion at top or bottom. Just often enough, though, you get an abrupt turn without much warning. Usually due to news or hitting an important S/R level, though. I have logged my 3+ years of experience, and another one beyond, BUT like many traders, especially in the beginning much time was squandered moving from system to system. True noobs, LISTEN, please. First, you MUST figure out yourself . If you can't watch the candles dance on M1 or 5 get the heck out of there. Unfortunately, in the beginning many want to trade and there are plenty of trades on M1, etc. You probably just won't win too many. I worked my way up to H4 which is great for information but just (maybe one or two) a few trades a week per pair doesn't work for everyone. It didn't make me comfortable, plus I was always resting when one of the good set-ups showed up. Oops again. Fortunately, I worked my way to MY (maybe not your ) sweet spot . . . M30/H1. There is enough going on for my personality but you really don't need to sit at the screen every second for hours on end. As has often been said, 1000 trades on one system/TF/pair etc is a huge knowledge multiplier. 1000 trades all over the map is just north of useless. Excellent trading to all and know thyself.

--- 帖子 #6926 ---
If you look carefully at HA candles and compare them to japanese candles, they don't actually hide the PA they show when that PA is confirmed. That's why they keep people in longer because they don't make them jump at every candle pattern that is coming up, they only turn a different colour when the candle pattern is confirmed. If you see for instance a pin bar yes its a sign it could turn around, but the colour will stay the same until the next candle confirms the pin bar. I have always traded on the smaller timeframes by not taking a counter trade until the htf looks like its starting to turn, it is something that I learned from someone's thread that was a great trader but sadly no longer posts and thats how he always managed to have a tiny stop loss with every trade and never had to add to a losing trade but added to winning trades only, a bit like the way omonisha does it although he didn't use the TDI only moving averages. By looking at the htf HA along with the htf TDI I can see if the trade I take on the lower timeframe is worth taking or not.

--- 帖子 #6928 ---
Good points on Higher TF.Most of my analyses is based on HTF.Generally good observations.I slightly disagree that HC candles react to patterns.They don't.They react to previous candle open and close high and low.There is no pattern recognition. 1- Open price: the open price in a Heikin-Ashi candle is the average of the open and close of the previous candle. 2- Close price: the close price in a Heikin-Ashi candle is the average of open, close, high and low prices. 3- High price: the high price in a Heikin-Ashi candle is chosen from one of the high, open and close price of which has the highest value. 4- Low price: the low price in a Heikin-Ashi candle is chosen from one of the low, open and close price of which has the lowest value. So candles of a Heikin-Ashi chart are related to each other because the open price of each candle should be calculated using the previous candle close and open prices, and also the high and low price of each candle is affected by the previous candle. So a Heikin-Ashi chart is slower than a candlestick chart and its signals are delayed If it works for you then continue. I guess I am a black sheep.I have aversion to it. regards

--- 帖子 #6962 ---
Thats not adding to losing trades in the way I mean, that is splitting a trade up into smaller amounts and trading it that way. If you get the entry right though the downfall of doing it that way is that you only have a quarter of the amount you were willing to risk riding on it. Thats why I look at every timeframe, larger and smaller to judge the best place for putting the trade in. That way I have a higher chance of getting it right first time and then if I have a pullback I am still in profit and the smaller timeframe will guide me where to add to the winning trade. If I get it wrong I'll know very quickly by the smaller timeframe and will take it out there.

My question for the veterans has to do with the close and open of the candle- I know Big E and other gurus on the higher timeframes wait for candle close to place a trade but do you guys wait for the setup candle to close on the lower timeframe and pull the trigger at the open of the next candle (warranted all other aspects of the trade have been observed)? or if there's momentum do you take the trade midway through the candle open/close?? Sometimes it feels like a catch 22, damned if you take it midway through and the candle pulls back significantly ("BUT THERE WAS MOMENTUM!) and damned if you wait until the candle close when it's already moved 60+ pips and the leg is exhausted. "great, here comes consolidation!"

One should study old chart to really marry with price actions (it s not repainted so it won't betray you, like TDI could turn around different from before and after candle closed, you know), TDI is there to support price actions and your actions, by the way, TDI is an indicator so it's lagging (followed by price actions). Hi NT Like LC said watch PA confirmed by lagging indicator TDI. Most uninformed think lagging is bad but lagging is there to provide guidance where PA may go.I don't pay attention to close candles but its behavior like spinning top? long wicks? tell a lot. Taking small losses is part of the game your job is to wait to zero in on trade that has MOST EDGE.Once that is achieved I most often add to my positions.Jesse Livermore did that like almost all the time. To me its important to admit when to get out.I don't set hard stop if I am on the computer.If PA is behaving contrary I get out but lots of times 15-20pip spikes are followed by PA going your way "fakies" so its not always good idea to close until you know if the move against you is real. This is something hard to explain how one can tell if the spike is real or not but I usually can tell. Anyway max $$=PA confirmed by TDI (provided you follow news and fundies) momentum going your way. I hope this helps I 'll share secret here but not everyone gets it.Focus on pairs that DON'T trend!Like one below.Same behavior on weekly.Now ask yourself how can you make money from this behavior. Looking at the chart would you confidently short at 97? Hell YES! what would be risk? 20% I think.Now given the beautiful set up would you increase lot or decrease? Well I usually go in full force because its obvious great opportunity! You see where I am going with this?When you see a great set up you must milk it and not so great ones small lots.

The pipcount doesn't change much while there is one long, one short on the same pair, only a pip or two caused by the spread. That -426 will stay there until I either exit or add another trade to the mix, one one, long or short. If that trade was successful the number would shrink but immediately bounce back to -426 when I exited the trade, same as if the trade failed, the number would grow, -430, -440, stopout and back to -426 again. I think the nedge has the effect of protecting capital but it also means there is no gain as well, it's not worth it. My broker allows me to place take up to 4 profit levels on a trade position at any one time but also allows to ask it to automatically move my stoploss to breakeven once a certain amount of pips have been reached and also to put a trailing stoploss on once a certain amount of pips have been reached. Basically it acts as a EA position manager and automatically takes profit levels and closes trades without me having to manually manage it myself. My broker is FXPro in the UK using their Ctrader platform, I use MT4 just for charts... Usually in my setup I have two profit levels taking 25% off each time while moving my stoploss to the prior TP level and trail the remaining 50%. So once TP1 is hit move stoploss to BE, once TP2 is hit then move stoploss to TP1 and then trail remainder.

--- 帖子 #7148 ---
Endless BS documentation...? Unfortunately, yes, that part is true. But, look at it from the perspective of the broker wanting to validate your identity to keep your account secure. Then it's not such a bad thing. And they give US clients 200:1 leverage, not that that means you have to use it... but, because the leverage allowed is 4x higher than the 50:1 that's allowed in the US, that means you can trade the same position sizes with 1/4 of the required margin deposited and keep the other 3/4 of your trading capital in something like a saving account in the US. Then if the broker does happen to go bankrupt, they disappear with 1/4 the dollar amount that a US broker would disappear with due to the higher required margin in the US. Again, a bit of research, a few demo accounts to see if the offshore broker fits well with your trading personality. Then maybe a small $300-500 micro account that you can trade and try a few withdrawals from, again, to see if the broker meets your expectations. I'd PM you my broker but, you have to do the research to find one that is a good fit for you personally. Give it a shot... all you have to lose is lower required margin and 4x / the leverage offered in the US.... oh, and no BS rules about hedging or FIFO.

--- 帖子 #7225 ---
Just sharing this for other newbies. I have had very good results (PA going in the direction of my trades) with this system but my profit achieved is laughable. I have gone back and examined each trade to see what I can learn from my mistakes and here is what I came up with: -I need to set a better profit target. I think 50 pips target is reasonable assuming ADR is not below average and Tokyo channel is above 40 pips. I am going to be more conservative and count the first pip from the bottom of the first signal candle for long trades and vice versa. -If R:R is not 1:2 or higher, no trade -don’t be greedy and try to re-enter after profit target achieved without full analysis. -pay attention to supply/demand zones -be aware of double bottoms, divergence, head and shoulder and other things that may increase your success -Don’t trade just to trade. (I know this, yet I do it). Here is something I learned that gave me a lot more confidence. If you see bb squeeze (Bollinger band), look at the TDI direction and obviously do your regular analysis, most of the time PA will go in the same direction after breaking out of the band with force. (let me know anyone needs charts for this, I can find some examples after I get home from work).

--- 帖子 #7286 ---
You don't even need to have funds in the account, unless you use no stop loss. If you use SL, there's no valid reason why you should have in the account more cash than it is required to keep the position open and hold margin within your SL level. You can still have the $10K volume sitting out of the trading account, safe. You can use margin whenever you need it by transfer. If you use fixed SL (and have discipline), the extra volume on top of margin is practically useless - and it's exposed to SNB type stuff.

--- 帖子 #7480 ---
hey TSS - its easy [but i am still learning this] - you decide where wave 1 starts and ends and where wave 2 ends - then just fit a cirle for these three ends [big problem - mt4 scales these as ovals - so must fix scale somehow] so once you have the first circle move a copy to cover the ends of wave 2 - this now forecasts the end of wave 3 as some value(price/period) on this circle - notice it does not give exact period/price - the sharper the impulse move the further the price range etc repeat the process for the next wave - another idea is that the circles can change by a fib amount ... still working on it buddy

While it was a decent gain in jobs for the month, the number was below economists' expectations and is likely to muddy the picture for the Federal Reserve's historic decision to raise its key interest rate in two weeks. Economists surveyed by CNNMoney projected that the economy would add 207,000 jobs. Wages grew 2.2% i n August, about in line with expectations but well below the Federal Reserve 's 3.5% target. Wage growth has been missing during the U.S. economic recovery from the recession, and it's also a key measure of inflation -- something that's been absent and that the Fed badly wants to see. Overall the job numbers in August add more uncertainty surrounding a potential rate hike from the Federal Reserve in two weeks. Fed officials have said they wanted to see key economic data like the jobs report before deciding on a rate hike. Although the U.S. economy has been good, this report is not a resounding victory for the American economy. What is missing from 5.1 rate is how many Americans are out of labor force basically stopped looking for job or can't find one. about 90 million. What I think is happening is an artifact of the way that unemployment is measured. In the standard measure, the U3 measure, you must be in receipt of unemployment insurance in order to be counted as unemployed. And in the US this usually stops at 26 weeks of unemployment thus the ART of Counting begins or political spin continues. Basically once your 26 weeks ends up you seize to exit as statistic of jobless.

--- 帖子 #7698 ---
I trade PA+Fundamentals.Indicators come after PA. Lets break this down Take UC for example 3280-33 is resistance zone =crude 44-45 Establishing this as resistance then one can confidently build positions on short side since Canadian dollar is heavily influenced by oil (fundemetal) Oil has been ranging last 3months or so which translates UC ranging as well. TDI allows better entry for me but I often take trades without it by simply looking at PA. You noticed LK often takes divergence trades and not all of them supported by TDI but she knows porcupine candles already are solid sign posts coupled with Div and she rolls in a trade. Not saying TDI is not useful but more you trade better you become identifying good opportunities.S/R to me is crucial.IF TDI says sell cross case of AU at 6920 then one has to make objective decision that PA is at support and is OVERSOLD despite of TDI pointing south on ALL TF trade was low probability hence should be avoided.You see there is discretion.One can't blindly take every signal. Its also important to understand what exactly is TDI Its basically 3 MA's and we all know moving average presents itself after Price goes certain distance.So Price is primary and MA's are reflection of price.Well since we already established TDI as MA's then it does not recognize where price is in relation to support and resistance ,RN and Daily Open or ADR. This is why by simply creating this system as EA it will fail. This is where you as trader comes in because trading is always discretionary. Regards

--- 帖子 #7763 ---
Guys just want to share this and its the heart of trading in my view. Most trading books always say "trend is your friend" follow trend and all that usual platitudes. What they are not saying that trending trends requires larger accounts and 15-30% DD when trend goes into a correction. Well lets say you are long on UC going with the trend at 3250 and price drops to 30.75.WEll do you exit with good size loss or stay in it "trading the trend" but lets say price drops to 1.29 are you still in it? drops another 100pips to 1.28 Now you are in panic is the trend reversing and you are stuck at the top or into a deep correction and now you are at 30% dd at breaking point. You see they never tell you this reality! So RANGE is where the money is if you are typical retail trader and not a bank or hedge fund. Trend traders scare shit from the word RANGE but seriously 70-80% of forex is in range and this can be backed up with solid statistics. I have made over 50% equity last month trading RANGE

--- 帖子 #7821 ---
Hi Sib It does not indicate buy or sell but gives you heads up. UJ ADR is about 110. Example day open at 20.10 and went to 2080 then one can conclude 80% of the move roughly on bull side has already taken place hence going long after 80% of daily ADR has less probability to succeed.Its a great way to quickly see that being late buyer or seller does not have good probability to succeed. Take also into account that during high impact news or fundemetal factor like recent Chinese stock market crash pairs can travel 5 times the distance.Recent crazy moves on G pairs were in 1k move in 1day. Does not happen often but one should be aware of fundies and news always.

Awchart, EJ looks bullish (price keeps making higher highs), wait for it to retrace to go long when TDI and APB confirmed, not worth it to go counter trend since it too bullish (look at H4 TDI on your chart where it crawling around 68 level). Take off guppy and put 50MA up and you will see price has been going along with some small retracements. You might ask what about divergence since there were a few came up? As mentioned a few times in my previous posts, no divergence works when H1 TDI&gt;68 or &lt;32. When a pair is trending, look for hidden divergence off S/R with TDI signal to go with the trend. I put on Synergy_Pro_APB for noobs to see with a better view where the yellow bridge crawling along 50MA...u need to be comfortable with what ever indies you use to be able to get the best out of them. I use clear charts more often as I can see real price open and close as I am very aggressive with G's pairs (in and out within 1/2hr to 2 hrs max) I don't pay attentions to TMS 10EMA dashboard nor TDI Angleator, however, they are very useful for quick glance and yes it s safe to go in a trade with those support (buy only when all arrow blue/green and sell only when all arrows are red and of course when TDI APB confirmed). Important to pay attention to price to see where last swing high/low is, did it make higher or lower? is support/ resistant nearby? what did price do previously around those S/R levels,...what else can be treated as basis fx? tell me... When you can't see clear PA that means it's in choppy zone, best and safe to stay out! Now, pls take a look at EU and do the same analysis to ask yourself if it good and sound to go short? I noted that EJ EU don't give me good signals everyday like EA GA GJ and sometimes, it'd better not to get in if it s not within our plan/rules ( you should have a trading plan if you have not had one) Don't get in a trade and worried since it did not meet all your rules in the first place, that cause stresses. Delete anything (indies) off your charts if they are not contributing to your decisions to get in and stay with your trades. Hope all makes sense. Have a nice weekend. Lkc

excellent vid LK - thnx 4 posting ... there are 2 very important things in this.... 1. if you have any trading system with the edge [like we claim it with M30 TMS+PA] each trading result will still be random &lt;- this is why noobs should forget about everything and just practice entries first [LW knows wat she is talking about]. If you win or lose the next 5 or whatever trades it means ABSOLUTELY NOTHING ... you will still win in the long run once you have everything in place (assuming you in fact have the edge) [...and NO - money management alone will not/cannot give you the edge - a common sales pitch - lookup Hanover's posts on this and more] 2. First mastering Demo [paper] trading is a key psychological first/last step. You should first be able to grow your demo trading - experience the feeling of detachment from the trading psychology because the last ultimate step is to return to this state of mind once you have mastered your demons - DO NOT disregard this step so quickly ... Big E knew this exactly which is why he said it one trader can not give/make another trader a 'winning system' - there are no short-cuts - the edge is more than a fixed set of rules - green/over/red etc

Based on the performance of the U.S. economy alone the Federal Reserve should raise interest rates because the unemployment rate has fallen to a level often associated with full employment. Wages are on the rise, the housing market is steady and manufacturing and service sector activity is expanding. The emergency conditions that warranted the zero interest rate policy is no longer in place and in turn, it is time to raise interest rates. However the Fed does not operate in a vacuum and between the volatility in international equities, the dovishness of the ECB, and the dovish bias of other central banks, it will be difficult for Janet Yellen to pull the trigger. 60% of economists surveyed by Bloomberg are still looking for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates next week but Fed fund futures are pricing in only a 30% chance of a move. It will be a difficult decision for the central bank and for this reason we expect investors to reduce their exposure to long dollar positions ahead of Thursday's rate decision . In other words, the dollar should weaken in the front of the week. Even if the Fed hikes, the rally to be short lived with choppy trading to follow because we expect tightening to be accompanied by lower guidance. One rate hike is all we are looking for from the U.S. central bank this week and they will go out of their way to ensure that the market understands this trajectory." Entire article is well written and worth reading.

--- 帖子 #7923 ---
Even if you are not Elliot Wave trader its always good idea to understand how price behaves. ABCD 123 patterns are most profitable and they are part of EW.You may have traded EW waves and not even know it. Idea to sell the rallies and buy the dips derives from wave theory. Wave 3 is always the strongest and longest. Not trying to change this system but knowing how PRICE behaves is critically important.An artist trying to draw human figure without anatomy knowledge with struggle vs one who knows basic skeleton. To me its important to understand what price does and then apply methods like this system to milk it.

Hi everyone, Great thread. I have tried to see if I can find the reasoning somewhere in this thread but no luck.....is there any reason why pips are reported by totaling all the entries vs. the average price in and average price out? I personally think that gives a better indication of what was really made on the trade. I.E. you could enter 3 lots on one entry and make 100 pips and enter 20 lots on another entry and make 10 pips claiming 110 pips when the reality is the average true pips made per lot is 22. Again, just curious. Thank you.

--- 帖子 #8104 ---
Thank you for your reply. I know it can be done, I do it....never doubted you guys or that you are all making pips / percentage increases on your accounts / gains. Percentage gains are good; however, looking at the average pips made on a trade is, in my humble opinion, the best way to see what someone has really done on the trade. Some people with tiny accounts may go for massive percentage gains, using lots of leverage and high risk to grow their account quickly, others with large accounts may use zero margin and risk .5% per trade so looking at things from a percentage gain stand-point can sometimes be skewed as well. Average pips based on all entries in and out on a trade is the most accurate in my humble opinion. Carry on and good luck everyone.
