--- 帖子 #8112 ---
Gents, I appreciate your points, not trying to create a situation here, believe me, I can see how valuable this thread is to many. My point is it's fine to see the entry and exit points on your chart; however, with no knowledge of lot sizes (and I don't think anyone should provide this information as it is personal) then seeing the entries can be misleading because as stated previously the first entry could be for 20 lots, then the last, and best entry up top could be for 1 lot, so no one has a clue really where you true average entry would be. See chart below. If your first entry for much bigger size is down lower then that tiny size at the top is insignificant to the overall trade and shows that the trade went significantly against you before you profited because the main entry was lower. Knowing the average price entered would show a true 'entry' because it would average out position sizing. Most software does this automatically for you. No need to reply to this post, just food for thought.

The difference is set of behavior patterns .Winner is conditioning themselves to repeat what worked and repeat enough that it gets hard wired in the brain.I am sure LK,GS see DIV's like nothing almost effortless however just seeing not enough they act upon on it.They know probability of being right is greater then being wrong provided PA agrees. In basic form every successful trader has set of criteria that if meant trades are taken without hesitation. --- 帖子 #8241 ---
Yeah, I think that's just the way that one works. Once you close the trade, it goes back to "zero", thus it only runs while the trade is open. After you close the position, you can double click on the pipcounter, delete it (don't worry, it'll come back), then use the text tool in MT4 to enter the total pips that you got and take a screenshot. When you're done, double click and delete the number you entered with the text tool, switch time frames from say, 30 to 15 and back to 30 and the pipcounter re-appears for your next trade. Sounds overly involved but, it takes less than a minute to do. That's how I do it.

Great. Was just thinking... you don't even have to delete the pips counter. You could leave it in there at zero and just use the text tool to enter the number of pips that you closed the trade for and have two sets of numbers. You'll know what it means, and that's the point. Also, you could take a quick screenshot just prior to closing the trade, then you'll have the number on the pip counter. Although in a fast moving market that could change by the time you take the screenshot and close the trade. Just a couple of other options.

Hi Alex Allow me to sum up trading simply. Price goes from support to resistance and reverse.In between traders make their entries.Does not matter the method if you understand Price Action. TMS is focusing on entries TDI cross +PA They are basically 2 types of traders. Ones that wait until price reaches extremes or key S/R and the other which just follow price. In my understanding TMS is about following price.Advatage of this method is that opportunities are plenty. Nobody here complains that they can't find trades.Daily is difficult to trade because it requires greater SL and DD but 30min is perfect average pip distance of 50pips.Make 200pips a week and you are golden. To GS 200pips is a hiccup Focus making simple entries In addition pay attention to major news events.Yellen speaks tomorrow for example.Being aware of news should be part of trading like breathing oxygen.Its that important. Anyway thought you may want to know why....

A technical momentum indicator that compares the magnitude of recent gains to recent losses in an attempt to determine overbought and oversold conditions of an asset. It is calculated using the following formula: RSI = 100 - 100/(1 + RS*) My MA signal is 5 from 7 again same idea. Test both default and mine and see what you like.Reason I posted the info because I want people to be aware that its not default..

--- 帖子 #8511 ---
Thanks for asking ballistical. There are couple of rules i learned and learning when trading price action pattern. Specially OB. [ Please be remember location is very important for price action pattern to work ] . If you look at any OB on any chart you will notice that they usually retrace near the previous candle hi/open close/lo. Or if there is any confluence like 200ema RN number within the previous candle. If can trade on retrace we can place logical emergency SL above/below that OB . Yes chance are there to miss trade but better no trade then loss high. If a bullish OB retraces and break previous candle low and vice versa then price action pattern gets invalidated. This way we minimized the risk . If we open position on the next candle open then risk will be too high as we are not sure whether this pattern will work or not. And we had an OB on EA H1 later on H4 both could be traded on retrace. About my comments, That was different scenario trader opened his position after around 140 pips move. Didn't wait for any retrace for that kind of move. It was H1 chart. Where to hide SL? A 50% retrace will be -70pips. Too much risk. That is why i commented does he have to trade must of that move. We need to protect our SL. And you know what he wrote next price almost hit his SL. Sorry for my poor explanation Here i draw a pic for you and all to understand how i want to trade a OB.

Hi LK, Yesterday was one of my favorite days to harvest pips, however does not ALWAYS work, but there is VERY HIGH chance to double your account in these special days and I will tell you what these days look like. ( however as I said, sometimes does not work, so it just helps you to tighten your SL and increase your RRR , it is not a holy grail. ) I just have to say that I don't scalp in 5 minutes or any low time frame, I just jumped to 5 minutes to show the clear entries and exits. My time frame starts from M15 ( and this one is just for entry ) but I will find OB and OS in higher TFs ) Regarding yesterday positions : In picture below I saw there is a plenty of space between green line ( around 1.6015 which is pivot line and the daily open price. Usually pivot line attracts the price, so when the price does not touch the pivot and moves straight to the support or resistance lines, the elastic band is stretching more and more. more stretching, more fly ! Attached Image (click to enlarge) In this kind of special days, price most of the time turns back from second R2 / S2 levels which R2 is the highest thick blue line in the picture. Around these areas, I look for divergences for entry. Then I look for PA to add positions if needed. For SL , easy ! , just place 20-30 pips above S2 , depends on your position size and your entry. For exit follow the Support / Resistance / Pivot lines and BRN . The main Target is PIVOT line ( green line ) . But if I say that I always use strict rules for entry and exit , so I'm wrong. In this dynamic market, you must be dynamic. Definitely having seen many PAs in these years, it helps me a lot to do without thinking. So many of things come from the guts and experience. Believe me, your strategy is much more safer and much more mechanical than mine. You can trade your strategy everyday, but for the special days like yesterday, there is only few opportunities in every month. However my usual and everyday strategy is more or less same as yours: PA, Pivots, Round numbers, Divergence. Happy to see you and other members strong and reliable strategies and illustrations and pipful results. I always like to learn new techniques at your thread. Hope I could explain well

--- 帖子 #8581 ---
hi Long, Normally when spotting divergence and M30 H1 TDI is safe which is 68&lt;TDI&gt;32 and@ S/R, you can enter any time seeing price making good progress toward the direction of your trade (such as if you intend to go long, price has to make higher high higher low, and vice versa for short), or safer to wait for confirmed candle to complete, however, I usually enter in the middle of it if I see PA is ready In this GN case, price is facing DOL ( revisit so hope it will get thru) like it currently do. I entered with my aggressive style (spotting the apb made same low but created higher high, TDI turned up) Look at closer view from my GN chart, I circled many pin bars, that sign was telling me bears running out...get ready for a reverse...but won't be until TDI up and not in oversold area... Lots of thing to be considered if you follow my agrressive style, also dividing your entries into smaller lots help ... If you are too worried about DOL, don't enter too close to it as it tend to retrace and kick you out then go up again, better to wait for it to go thru DOL and get in at retrace. Updated: exited all @2.40am est when saw price could not make higher high

--- 帖子 #8660 ---
The % success of advanced patterns (bats, cyphers, gartleys, etc) is probably something that you could google search. However, the issue isn't with the indicator. The indicator is doing what it's supposed to do. It's the opinion of the traders in the market at the time that the pattern "completes"... it's the traders actions at those levels that dictate whether or not the indicator is forced to repaint. So, the indicator just shows you a potential turning point, whether or not price actually turns at that point is a whole different matter.

--- 帖子 #8706 ---
Correlation and cross pairs are 2 different things. Correlation is when 2 currencies move either in (usually) negative correlation or positive correlation, that correlation can change at any time price wants to do something different which is why there is a site to tell you what the latest correlation stats are. Cross pairs are where the actual price of 2 currency pairs make up the price of the third so it cannot do anything else, mathematically speaking. If I divide the price of GU by the price of AU it will give me the price of GA, likewise, divide the price of EU by the price of AU it will give me the price of EA. They therefore have to be moving in different directions to make it worthwhile trading or not being too choppy if both GU and AU are going up at the same time, at roughly the same speed the price of GA isn't going to change much. You can usually tell at a glance which trade would be best to take by the glancing at the pairs that make up the cross pair price.

In fact if there are no revisions next month and payroll growth rises by less than 200k in October and November, a December rate is also off the table. In September, Janet Yellen made it very clear that they are want to see further job growth but instead of gaining strength, labor market activity deteriorated significantly last month. As a result, rate hike expectations have collapsed with Fed fund futures now pricing in only 30% chance of tightening before the end of the year compared to 45% chance pre-NFP. So it should be no surprise that the dollar adjusted as well. However by the end of the North American session the greenback clawed back its losses on the premise that of the large number of Federal Reserve officials scheduled to speak next week many will continue to throw their support behind 2015 tightening. But talk is cheap when data is weak . Only 142k jobs were created in the month of September and the August figures were revised down to 136k from 173k. More importantly average hourly earnings growth was flat, which was much weaker than the market anticipated and while the unemployment rate remained unchanged the participation rate dropped to its lowest level in 38 years. In order for the bulls to return to the dollar we need more than talk from U.S. policymakers. U.S. data needs to surprise positively and in very big ways. Non-manufacturing ISM is the most important U.S. economic report on the calendar next week. The Fed minutes are also scheduled for release and that may have a more significant impact on the dollar. EUR/USD soared above 1.13 intraday on the back of the weaker U.S. labor market report before settling back near 1.12 . Today's price action was driven exclusively by the market's appetite for U.S. dollars because Eurozone data surprised to the downside. Producer prices came out much weaker than expected with PPI falling for the second month in a row by -0.8%, the largest decline in 7 months. Deflation is not a major concern for ECB officials but the recent trend of inflation reports combined with low commodity prices adds pressure on the central bank to ease. Additional easing is not necessary at this time but these weak reports along with softer data from Germany will keep euro from rallying too much. There are only a handful of Eurozone economic reports scheduled for release next week - none of which are extremely market moving. We have revisions to the PMI Composite, German Industrial Production and the Trade Balance. ECB President Draghi is also scheduled to speak but given that the forum is the Art on Site Inauguration, he may not touch on the economy or monetary policy. For the first time in 11 trading days, sterling ended the North American session with some decent gains versus the U.S. dollar . We are looking for a further near term rally in GBP/USD because when the pair turns, the reversal can be strong but the sustainability of gains hinges on theBank of England who has a monetary policy announcement next week. While no changes are expected the BoE now releases the minutes at the same time as their statement and the number of dissenters as well as the overall tone of the central bank could have a big impact on how sterling trades. Last month, only 1 member of the monetary policy committee voted to raise interest rates and the central bank as a whole did not sound overly concerned about global developments or domestic conditions. While they lowered their Q3 growth forecast, they made no mention of the downside surprises in the PMIs and instead said productivity has begun to increase and core inflation may be firming. They believed that domestic demand would help erode spare capacity in the coming year. On balance their comments suggested that they are still looking to raise rates next year but want to see what the Fed does first. All 3 of the commodity currencies moved higher today but the shallowest gains were in AUD/USD. Next week is a big week for the Australian dollar with PMI services, the trade balance report and a Reserve Bank of Australia monetary policy announcement on the calendar. Given the recent improvement in economic data including last night's retail sales number and this week's PMI manufacturing index, the RBA is not expected to lower rates. While the Bank of Japan is not expected to change monetary policy, Japanese data has taken a turn for the worse as the stimulative impact of Abenomics begins to fade. Mostly professional says, use 1-3 % for every position, ok , I partially agree, but assume you have hard earned your money penny by penny and you are willing to lose $100 for each position. Ok this is mathematical part, but DO YOU REALLY READY TO LOSE $100 OF YOUR HARD EARNED PENNIES IN ONE SINGLE TRADE, EVEN IF YOU FOLLOW THE %1-3 CLASSIC RULE ? In my opinion the percentage must be multiplied to the trader's tolerance and acceptance of losing trade which is like a finger print and is different from a trader to another one. If you are scared even by following 1% rule, then as Davit said, " your brain will be scared, as a result will do stupid things ". So it's better to reduce the size maybe to 0.5% 0.3% for every trade to find your comfort zone . So when you open some position, you can freely and dynamically wait, response and make the best judgment until closing whether you lose or win by the end. In either way, you are still in your comfort zone. If you open some positions, and check them every minute and watchdog the positions and can't sleep well, you are most likely to lose your money, not because you are in wrong side of the market, the only reason is because: " Scared brain does stupid things. "

ok - i need to explain a few things first - the first thing is the idea of cause &amp; effect - the easiest way to tinks about that is to take two currencies [Bicore] - the idea still applies to more currencies [tricore / quadcore etc] say you have EUR and USD then pretend you can make two pairs from this EU and UE [makes no sense in reality but good for understanding ] - now wat you can not say is if UE goes down 'then' EU will go up - this is the wrong way to tinks about it - you have to say if UE goes down EU will go up at the 'same time' - there is no cause &amp; effect happening [i am only look'n @ this from tech level not fundie] now things get more hard to tinks about when its tricore - say EUR / USD / AUD - and you must understand something first - say i give you the price for EA [say its 2.00000] but you can not look @ EU and AU charts - even thou you can always combine EU and AU at any tick to give EA [EA's legs - look @ this http://www.babypips.com/school/high-...oss-pair.html] you can not build their charts from that info - you are missing one bit of info - there are 50 billion different charts for EU and AU that will still give you EA@2.00000 - but - if i give you say AU and EU then you can build EA price by price - now you can see there is no cause &amp; effect working here - there cant be cause theres no independence pair by pair you can now move to quadcore and i will show you a easy way to see this and i use this in my trades theres just one more thing i have to explain the type of intermarket corr traders use is explained @ babypips http://www.babypips.com/school/under...s-it-gets.html there may well be cause &amp; --- 帖子 #8973 ---
Hi OuterWest, you have voiced your displeasure in many occasions regarding the usage of acronyms in this thread. You are right that this may cause new traders some confusion but they can ask questions. If they struggle with these acronyms they may use google to do a search and learn them. Each profession has its own language and so dose Forex. When a group of people interact in any type of social setting especially via the internet, they form their own language and abbreviations to communicate with each other and bond. Many traders post their trades right after closing it and may have another trade open or looking at possibly entering another one as a result they want to make a quick post and get back to trading. There have been many occasions ( in another thread) that I missed a trade due to making a full detailed post. I don't think that everybody can teach since teaching is something that you either have it or not. The issue that I am noticing with this thread which is troublesome is the lack of posting of losing trades. This may cause new traders to think this method has no losers which isn't the case. As we know, there are days that the market just chops you to pieces and those are the days that all of the sudden everybody just goes away. One can learn from losing trades just as much as wining trades. I have picked up some great tips which has made me move away from 5M and 15M charts to the 30M and higher time frame charts which is less taxing on me. The multiple entry technique is a nice addition which I am forever thankful to all the great contributors and there are many fantastic, sharing and caring traders on this thread and I salute them all. I have no intention in getting into a back and forth banter with anyone since I have better things to do with my life. Happy pipping to all.

--- 帖子 #9109 ---
I like to share something that may be controversial the way you trade but its just my opinion and you are free to dismiss. About MA's or EMA's There is lot of talk about bounce from this EMA or another.Most relevancy of EMA is on daily Weekly TF and most important 200 because its institutional barometer.On lower TF its relevancy is pure coincidence.Price did not "bounce" from 10EMA Price action happened to hit that MA and same true on all EMA's on lower TF. Throw a Guppy "rainbow" MA on the chart and I can guarantee price will hit 1 or several on every move. Just keep perspective that TDI is Ma's based hence it already is doing its intended job. That's it.If it works go ahead continue the way you see PA but I can assure you guys who buy/sell in millions moving price can care less about any minor MA regards

But several ECB officials worry that more measures will be needed to raise inflation, as consumer prices in the eurozone decreased by 0.1% annually in September, the first decline since the program began. Investors are increasingly betting that the ECB will either lengthen the duration of the bond-buying program or increase the amount of monthly purchases either at its policy meeting this Thursday, or in December. Either move is likely to weigh on the common currency. The euro has mostly traded between $1.08 and $1.14 since May, a range which has tightened to around $1.13 since late August. The ECB appears to make efforts to rein in the common currency whenever it strengthens to $1.14, said Dave Pierce, chief strategist at GPS Capital Markets, Inc., a Salt Lake City-based firm that provides foreign-exchange services to corporations. “The ECB really has a strong bias to keeping the euro weak right now, allowing the eurozone countries to be more competitive in the world markets,” Mr. Pierce said. “There’s a clear target for the euro for the ECB; the euro will stay below that $1.14 level.”

--- 帖子 #9242 ---
It actually a deeper subject. How does one measure success. I trade in units. Monthly I unit includes 4 weekly unit Weekly includes several batch trades average of 50trades Daily 10-15 trades You may lose 1 weekly unit but win 3 weekly ones making your monthly unit a +positive gain. When you approach like this your individual trades becomes less important .Focus is on bigger picture. This way you approach trading from looking down from airplane instead of top of coke battle Single or multiple loses means little because approach is grouping in units.This way it takes the psychological difficulty most people have about taking a loss.I took 17 losses this month so far and close to 30% gain. Its not about single trade. That's why TMS30 should be measured on 100+trades.

--- 帖子 #9309 ---
Also.... when you reinstall MT4, do NOT install it in the default program files folder. Something with WinOS security messes with MT4 when installed in the program files folder. when you reinstall it, create a new folder on the C:/drive and put it there. Call it something like "C:/My_MT4". Install to that folder and that could resolve a lot of problems for you.

Hi Shadownet, good question from you and good answer from Griffinssoul mentioned about my rules: - no trade entered when TDI is below 32 or above 68 or you will suffer big DD. - do not trade into DOL, 200MA, S/R at 1st touch (rules stated on 1st post) - after divergence formed, price usually retrace to make higher low (bullish divergence) or lower high (bearish divergence), therefore, your stop loss should be placed accordingly, it's up to you to play, I can't tell you exact pips as it depends on the pair, the swing high low and the range of that moment even though my intial SL/PT 50/50 but I usually adjust as trade in progress. Best to take divergence bounced off/ at support or resistant and where TDI not @OB/OS areas. - I have Synergy_Pro_TDI which I found it more conservative than normal TDI as it does not let me enter a trade too early around overbought/oversold (68/32 levels). I have low tolerant to bear big loss or staying in a losing trade if I monitored it, I would accept that I was wrong and exited my trade if market condition changed when spotting price making higher low and no support nearby (if I was in a sell) and vica versa for a buy . I could exit and re-enter it if a new signal showed up. My largest SL could be upto 130pips if I saw H4 confirmed and I didn't have chance to be at my desk.

--- 帖子 #9542 ---
Thanks for your post, there are many things that you need to consider before taking a trade. 1.) What does the higher time frame H4 say about the current trend? Up or down? 2.) How far (pips) can this trade go in my favor? 3.) What is my SL and TP levels? Are they 1:1 or better? 4.) Are there any support or resistance levels that may stop my trade from going in my direction? 5.) Which session does this pair move the most? 6.) Any news that may effect my trade within the next 30 minutes? 7.) Always honor your SL. Once the answers to the above question are in sync with your trade direction then you may take a trade.

--- 帖子 #9565 ---
yeah it s kinda, but not exactly what I understood but it was a good pull back and price was making higher low and higher high and it worked . Good shot . PCRF( in my opinion) Includes 3 candles: 2nd candle has to stick out and 3rd candle close below 1st candle, and we can enter of the break out of 1st candle. It works with trend pullback and off S/R In the pic I post on ECAD ( that trade I entered on H4, so pls ignore it), just showing you where I circled 2 pullback, 1st circle reversed when hit 200ma, 2nd cirle pullback went well. If you noticed on EJ m30 chart you post, right before your entry long, there was a PCRF bounced off DOL but since price was stepping up after bullish divergence, so if we entered that PCRF for a short it would fail Here what I found from Phx62's files: PCRF 1. Candle in the direction of the trend 2. Followed by a lower candle that sets a lower low and then pulls back leaving a long wick 3. Followed by a 3rd candle that may or may not change colour but sets a higher low and is usually an inside bar 4. Followed by an entry candle that breaks above the previous inside bar candle = Entry

There is a limit to how many positions are opened and is account percentage based. 3.) There is a hard SL and that is based on account percentage as well. Once it is reached all trades are closed. 4.) Once in profit, positions in greatest profit get their SL moved to BE to preserve capital. 5.) My +303 pips on these trades may have less dollar value than someone else's one +50 pips trade.

--- 帖子 #9660 ---
This is from Emmanuel. I just copied and pasted for you. You can replicate the TDI using any platform provided RSI indicator. Here is how to do it. How to replicate the TDI using the standard RSI indicator. The Traders Dynamic Index aka TDI is actually 3 moving averages of the RSi data. The default parameters are: the TDI Price Line PL green line is a SMA(2) of the RSI(period 13, Close Price). Then the TDI Trade Signal Line red line is a SMA(7) of the PL green line. The TDI Market Base Line MBL yellow line is a SMA 34 period of the PL green line. You can replicate these using the platform standard RSI indicator: Steps: 1. Create RSI in a new window. Set the parameters to Period 13 and use the Close Price, and set the color to None, this will not show the RSI line. 2. Select and drag the Moving Average indicator into the sub-window as the RSI. Set the MA period to 2, Simple, Close, color = Green, and the most important last parameter is to, Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. 3. Select and drag the Moving Average indicator into the same sub-window as the RSI. Set the MA period to 7, Simple, Close, color = Red, and the most important last parameter is to, Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. 4. Select and drag the Moving Average indicator into the same sub-window as the RSI. Set the MA period to 34, Simple, Close, color = Yellow, and the most important last parameter is to, Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. Note: all three settings must be Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. The above setup should now show the TDI replicated with these default parameters: RSI_Period = 13 RSI_Price = 0 RSI_Price_Line = 2 RSI_Price_Type = 0 Trade_Signal_Line = 7 Trade_Signal_Type = 0 Market Base Line = 34 Market Base Line Type =0

--- 帖子 #9722 ---
Thanks for the video GS. Let me share a story with you: There once was a man (John) with a wife (Linda) and two kids living in California, USA. John and Linda both worked and made about $12000.00 a month. John got interested in trading. After many years of sweat and tears, he finally started to make money in trading. John saved and grew his trading account to a point that he started to replace his income. So John quit his job and became a full-time trader. After a while John took out his retirement money and added it to his trading account. Now his trading account stood at $400,000.00 and he was making a return of 5% per month so his monthly income grew to $20,000.00 per month. Linda quit her job as well. As their income grew so did their spending habits. Bigger house, shiny new BMW, Big boat, HD motorcycle and nicer everything. Now fast forward ten years. John continued to make 5% per month. After 10 years of trading, John is completely burnt out and hates to trade, yes it will happen. He needs a minimum of $20,000.00 to continue living his current lifestyle. If he had compounded part of his winnings for those 10 years and reduced his spending habits, he could have retired by now. "Compound interest is the eighth wonder of the world. He who understands it, earns it ... he who doesn't ... pays it." Albert Einstein

--- 帖子 #9803 ---
Hi, Davit. I think there's no way to change the RSI settings (RSI period,.. etc.) in Angleator. It seems it uses hard corded default settings of TDI-RT-Clone.ex4 (or TDI Red Green.ex4). Even if we change the TDI settings in your chart, it's not reflected to Angleator. To change the TDI settings (for example, to match Synergy Pro's) in Angleator, I think we need to edit TDI-RT-Clone.mq4 accordingly and recompile it. I found Synergy_Pro_TDI.ex4 is not supported. If we change its name to "TDI-RT-Clone", MT4 just crashes. The only way to use Synergy Pro settings is to edit/recompile TDI-RT-Clone.mq4. Please correct me if I am wrong.... Thanks.

--- 帖子 #9930 ---
If you are asking regarding my MM on my multiple entry trades, here it is. I risk a certain percentage of account per trade and my trade size varies depending on the ADR of the traded pair. Number of trades taken on a pair is predetermined, I don't set a hard SL or TP level and have stopped moving my SL to BE. My R:R varies from 1:1 to 1.5:1. As far as targets I have a target in mind based on S/D and Fib pivots and like my trade to run as much as possible but may close a trade early due to fundamental changes on the traded pair, big upcoming news or intuition. I am still experimenting with this style of trading. On my scalping trades I use a hard SL and TP is manual and SL is moved to BE after I am in profit by some pips. On TMS M30 trades, I use a hard SL and my TP is usually area of confluence.

--- 帖子 #9983 ---
Hi Davit, could you let us know what happened to this trade as price went completely the opposite direction. I think the TMS method is great, but my worry with this thread &amp; other thread is the Survivorship Bias. Definition: Survivorship bias , or survival bias , is the logical error of concentrating on the people or things that "survived" some process and inadvertently overlooking those that did not because of their lack of visibility. It's great that everyone posts their winning trades, but it would also be helpful for new traders learning this system to see some of the experienced traders of this system post their losing trades. There are often more trading lessons in how to take a losing trade and manage a losing trade than there are in just posting winning trades. I am not picking a fight or picking on you - just making an observation of this thread &amp; will hopefully encourage some other leaders of this thread to do the same. Thanks again for all the great input.

--- 帖子 #10058 ---
The yellow line on the TDI indicator is the MBL (Market Base Line) when green and red TDI lines are below it, it is safer to go short rather than long. Does this work 100% of the time? NO.. Your trade is a counter trend and it may work or may not. Your entry based on this trading system was a No Go for me. If you trade a pivot system only then your trade was OK but still a counter trend trade which is riskier.

--- 帖子 #10061 ---
Kubiasty, if you decide to take counter trend trades and into the DOL, I prefer that the distance to DOL from your entry be twice as much as your SL. For example, SL of 50 pips and then distance to DOL of 100.0 pips,this way your trade may have a better chance of survival but this is more of an advanced technique. This is from page one, post one by likica: "Rules: TDI green crossed red off S/R, trade away from Daily Open Line (DOL), 200 EMA, and weekly S/R"

--- 帖子 #10132 ---
Thanks likica, no I didn't have insider info. I had a SL based on account percentage which could have been hit. Trading without a SL (kill switch) is just gambling. Would I start building a position right before major news? NO WAY. But I am aware of the the fact that news may either help or kill my trade. I have come to embrace the fact that trading is just a probability game (RIP Mark Douglas). I am starting to become outcome indifferent in my trading. At times a bad setup may lead to a winner and vice versa. I take winners and losers in stride and just rinse and repeat. These mega pips gained are just a small percentage gained on my account (2-4% depending on the traded pair) and a loss would have been a dent in my account of (3-5% depending on the traded pair) and that is due to the fact that my TP is dynamic ( not set in stone) and my SL is static (fixed). For example, some may risk 2% in one trade with SL and TP of X pips and others may split entries but risk nearly the same 2%. Likica's one +50 pips trade may be worth more Dollars ($$$$) than my +740.0 pips .

Great results Shad I've got to say that I hate repeating (sound like a broken recorder or a mummy type), it shows that you did not read my prev posts or missed them to find the answers. Anyway, here's my answers: 1) How many pairs do you follow in your list and which one ? GA EA GN EN GJ EJ EU GU (sometimes checking GCAD ECAD, watching (no trade) on AU NU) 2) What is your Risk reward ratio with all pairs ? (In pips with each pairs specially G pairs) 50ps for initial SL/PT, then adjust them as trade in progress. Don't let your SL get hit, you have control over it (not your brokers unless you are not avail to monitor your trades), it's your job to watch PA and act accordingly, don't ask more, study old charts and watch live market and practise more to gain experience to build confidence. 3) What is your first look while searching trade ? have H1 of those pairs up on 1 screen all the time and if any of those @S/R with pin, price stalled, etc, act on M30, watch TDI avoid trade at overbought/oversold on the time frame you trade. 4) What is the role of News in trading ? Don't predict, watch charts (high/low) 15min after news out, no trade if PA looks confusing. 5) What is the confirmation to let your trade run or exit ? I m still learning to let my trades running, currently base on 1 or 2 of these lines to determine my exits. : S/R, TL, Fibs, m30ATR(7)for counter trend, H4 ATR(7)with trend Happy pipping!

--- 帖子 #10266 ---
Welcome to M30, Fbrand79. If you already traded with TMS method regardless what version you used, price actions are always 1st thing you look then indies or in this method we use TDI with APB to confirm. Some traders don't need Stochastic nor Awesome and it's ok, but I always have them on. I advised traders not to put more indies but put less if they need to learn to read price actions well specially how price reacts around S/R. Keep in mind that TDI crosses, divergence, hidden divergence won't work if PA not right or when TDI still at overbought (TDI&gt;68) or at oversold (TDI&lt;32). If you would like to learn how we trade here, please spend more time to read my charts and comments or from some super traders like Lastingwell, Griffinssoul, Omonisha, PipsNinja, Pips92, Josh, The Scorps,... Each of us have our own way but all based on PA &amp; TDI. Good luck and happy pipping.

--- 帖子 #10446 ---
I put a lot of levels on my chart and I m watching how price behaves around them. My chart looks not as clean as other seniors but those levels are there to serve me, so it's up to individual to want to leave them on or just want to draw them manually. I always pay respect to 1st touch of any level whether it s DOL or 61% or 50% or 38%, or 200ema, etc. It's the exit that need big improvement since we usually talk about good entries but that is not the whole story. It's good to do lots of research, however, IMO, review is more important as we need to know where we are at, then find out the way to get where we want to be. Here is a snapshot of my GA taken yesterday, we have experienced GA ranging within the Wide Range Bar (WRB), many traders would avoid trading the pair. I was playing around with PA crawling between 200EMA &amp; DOL, since there was space for my PT, I gave it a shot. Best entry should have been at the red arrow. I entered after spotting 2nd lower high following 2nd lower low without waiting for a red APB.

--- 帖子 #10476 ---
That's correct provide the signal you take is with the trend on M30. There are many way to exit such as S/R, trailing 1st PT @ATR(7) x 1, 2nd PT@ ATR X 2, 3rd PT exit when opposite signal appears, etc. If you study my posts, I take +50green for my trades very often. If you want to do the same, make sure to check if there s space for your PT (distance between your entry to next S/R) before entering your trade. Avoid buy if TDI is under 32(too bearish), avoid sell if TDI is over 68 (too bullish) unless you are really good at reading PA . You need to be firm (follow your plan) with your entries and be flexible with your exits which only come with your own experience. Give TMS at least 1 month with full attention to study (if you are not newbie to FX), then demo 3 months if profitable, go live after that.

Hi jmmn, no worries. To get back to the conventional candles, you would have to delete the Synergy APB indicator which would mean that the APB Arrows would disappear too. The pdf says that the arrows do not repaint. However, if you change your chart to a different time period and then go back, they reset and could change then. As with the APB indicator removing the arrows, I think its a good chance that it will remove the alerts too. Hope that helps jmmn.

--- 帖子 #10552 ---
Long read but worth the read, read and learn. There are reasons why profitable traders achieve the way that they do. Here are 10 powerful qualities of profitable traders that they share. 1. Clarity: They know what they want and they have a hunger for it. Everyone makes mistakes, including market wizards and highly successful traders. The difference is that they “learn” from each mistake and rarely repeat them. That’s because they have a clear idea of what they want; and they want it very much. Once they make a mistake, especially if it results in a loss, they double down not on the trade but on their efforts to follow-through with what-matters-most. When you want something with an intense desire, the true nature of your potential is realized through the fire in your passion. This emotional fixation tunes the body, mind and spirit to work singularly for anything it focuses on. As the saying goes, you become “hungry.” You “want it so bad you can taste it.” 2. A strong sense of purpose…the Big Why Profitable traders develop a strong sense of purpose. This is the real reason for making the effort, and it is well defined. The undisciplined person doesn’t know what they want; they often have no direction, can’t make a decision, are consistently changing, constantly looking outside themselves for the answer and are forever starting projects they never finish. 3. Goal setting and visioning Another characteristic these traders share relates to goal setting and creating a sensory-rich vision. The undisciplined have vague goals that they might, maybe, someday achieve. They are capable of sensory-rich images but apply it to doom-and-gloom scenarios. Achievers visualize their outcomes clearly and creatively using all their senses to taste, see, hear, touch and smell the goal. They create the emotion of winning, which takes the spark of purpose and turns it into a flame. 4. A positive sensory orientation Achievers have a positive sensory orientation. They expect to succeed. They see past accomplishments, no matter how small, as proof of the pudding—they did it before and can do it again. Profitable traders are not afraid of risks and trying new approaches. They never lose site of the goal. Each failure is a new and valued lesson that takes them closer to their goal. The undisciplined waste their time dwelling on past failures, and this often turns into reinforcement to stop trying. 5. A role model or mentor Self-disciplined traders have a role model and/or a mentor, someone whose advice they trust. Throughout history, great men and women have looked to a role model for inspiration and as an example of how to do it. The achiever studies the patterns of the successful trader, someone who is already achieving what they desire. The undisciplined look for the quick-fix models; they think it’s a gimmick, that it’s luck or who you know. These people resent the truly successful. They blame their lack of success on excuses; bad breaks, bad luck and/or bad parents, and see themselves as victims. 6. Self-assuredness The previous five characteristics help develop this one – self-assuredness. Heavy hitters are fueled by self-confidence. They have a strong belief in self and their ability. They know that they can do it. The undisciplined are hampered by self-doubt. Failure haunts them and fills their mind with fear and stifles their ability to take risks. 7. The ability to plan and organize The undisciplined have no clear game plan. The skill of prioritizing eludes them as they make endless lists they never get done. They are disorganized and waste time and energy chasing illusions. Achievers break goals into pieces and work with one job at a time. They prioritize their time and accomplish first things first. 8. The necessary education Heavy-hitting wizards get the knowledge required to make the game plan work. The undisciplined look for short cuts instead of dedicating time and effort on a proper education. They take a weekend course and become experts. To them, it is too much trouble to get it right; they lack patience. Winners identify the necessary knowledge and they acquire it, going back to school if necessary. They recognize the critical importance of learning how to do it right. 9. Patience The ninth characteristic of the peak performance wizard is patience. The undisciplined want everything now and can’t wait. They view time as the enemy and think it will be wasted if they don’t get on it right now, without the proper preparation, like starting a trading business without a business plan or entering a trade without a trading plan. All real achievers possess patience. They understand that true accomplishment takes time. Time does not intimidate this trader; in fact time becomes a tool. They know, as they are working on the goal, that each passing minute takes them closer to its achievement. 10. Persistence and perseverance Free Trading WorkshopPersistence and perseverance rank as tenth on the characteristic list. The undisciplined are driven by quick fixes, impulsive schemes and are at the mercy of greed and fear. As soon as the tick goes against them they panic, and their minds are no longer focused on what the charts are giving. They see only what the distortion will allow. They are easy quitters when the going gets tough. Big time achievers stick to their vision despite setbacks. They don’t give up when met with hardships or the negative opinions of others. Successful achievers are relentless and stubborn. They succeed against all odds, and when they are discouraged they draw inspiration and motivation from their sensory-rich vision. There you have it, 10 powerful qualities of profitable traders. Its your turn to learn and imbibe them. Written by Dr. Woody Johnson, Online Trading Academy Instructor

Likica, I took a similar trade on the AJ and bagged 40 pips. I've been testing some divergence indicators and have found a rather good RSI divergence indicator called "Divergence Petr 1" The indicator places a yellow dot at every low and a red dot at every high. Then, when there is a divergence, it draws the line in. It also draws in high channels and low channels, allowing for channel crossover trades. I've found that when there is a divergence detected, you wait for the cross of the 50 level and then enter there. I used the method on my AJ trade shown in the picture below. I'll also add the indicator so you can take it for a spin if you want. Moonie. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached File(s) Divergence Petr 1.mq4 65 KB | 340 downloads

--- 帖子 #10589 ---
. I don't really know if I understood your question clearly, I m guessing you want to scroll your chart backward to last week for example. Here the steps: From the top panel of mt4 where you see 'File', 'View', 'Insert', 'Charts,..., click on ' Charts' , a small long window appears, from that click 'Auto Scroll ' and ' Chart shift' to turn them off, it will allow you to go backward. When you want to go to current price, you click on those buttons again (turn them on) it will scroll your chart forward. Hope I have helped with your question. It would be easier if I could make a snapshot to show you by pictures but I don't know how to do it as there are 2 buttons on mt4 for a short cut where you click on a button with little backward red arrow and a button with small green triangle.

I accept the fact the Big News are either going to help or bust my positions. I wouldn't start building positions right before major News but a few days before is OK. Even if Big News don't stop you out but cause your positions to go into further DD what you should do then? You need to interpret the long term effect of News. Not all but some big News may start trends lasting thousands of pips. AUD News came out earlier showing a stronger Aussie job market which is good for its economy. CAD has a strong correlation to Oil due to its large Oil deposits and with Oil prices at historic lows things are not looking good for CAD. A big pop in Oil prices could help your positions. Who knows in this crazy world what is going to happen next but there are many things to consider when position building trading.

--- 帖子 #10746 ---
I just wanted you share some insight of my trading and something I do which I believe helped me to become more profitable and consistent with my Trading. First we should all have rules or a trade plan to follow and stick to. We should have them written out for example wait for a rejection off S + R or DOL or whatever you want as your rules! Then I number these rules. Once I enter a trade I will write the time and date of this trade and how many of my rules were included in my entry, for example rule 1, 5 and 9! Then at the end of the week/month I would look for which trade were successful and check the rules to these trades and the same with the negative trades. After some time you will begin to notice pattens that work better than other and you can filter down some of these trades and learn what is working and what is not... I have found this is a very productive way of analysing our trades and the rules we have set. It really help me so thought I would share maybe some of you will find this useful too

--- 帖子 #11071 ---
Be very strict when you draw trendlines to see if there is divergence or not, thats where quite a few people fall down when looking for it. Take your lines across the peaks of the indicator and then the corresponding price points there is no divergence there if you do it like that and when divergence is there when you do it, it is more likely to be a winner.

...print &amp; paste on nearest wall [like were you can see it when trading ] ... here is wat i do to make a rule for div - first you have a fractal... i use around 5 candles [cause we are using RSI(13)] - wait for a color change and so on the second fractal only have 5 candles to the left ... the right hand side is for your M30 TMS signal - finish by spotting a camel's back on the RSI - wait for candle close [this is a must for noobs!!!!!!] LW has said repeatedly we do not use the real time TDI ... if you are trading with a robot - and not watching - then the results appear to be the same in my back testing for the TDI versions i have tested - so it does not make a diff EDT: Opsss! --- 帖子 #11091 ---
No I have never abandoned the rule of trading away from DOL. For this GN trade, my initial profit target was 100p (and the distant from my entry to DOL covered that requirement), but I increased when I looked at TDI still deep straight down and felt more confident with the change when I looked left at the last swing expecting it could make it and it did make more. If you asked a different question (such as how can I learn from this?), you would learn more For all who are not sure, make it simple and treat DOL at its 1st touch of the day like a strong S/R, if you have a good PA and TDI confirms and it happens to go toward DOL, make sure there is enough space for your profit. Always look left too If anyone seeing yourself missing trading opportunities due to this rule , try to override it and see how many pips gone and never come back . Until you recognize and learn from your own mistakes, you know the value. I bet you are sitting in GU short which looks pretty bearish. Good luck

--- 帖子 #11409 ---
1st trade (short): better entry once price broke trendline 2nd trade (short): correct entry is the close of 3rd candle of Pull back candle reverse formation (PCRF). My trade "B" where I entered it late and got out when price pull back, "C" was my pending order got filled and went to my PT. 3rd trade (long): correct entry is the close of 3rd candle of PCRF. If you are still unsure what I referred as PCRF, there is a PDF file from paper clip (Phx62's style) I posted a while back for traders to study on one of the nice PA we use a lot here where price pull back and bounce off S/R. I pay attention to any pivots to see how price reacts around those levels, while watching where TDI heading. Some traders only pay attentions to pivots and ignore TDI that where they have to sit with big draw down or get out with a loss.

--- 帖子 #11696 ---
Hi J If I were to train new traders 1st off I would start them from perspective of how you feel about money . How you feel about it determines everything.Your tolerance to drawdown, Stop Loss, take profit. I have found that more you treat money as number, a tool, soldiers in army better you see possibilities.When you imagine how hard you earned that deposit how many hours you had to sweat making it then your decisions in trading effect directly. So start from your mind 1st. Book that is remarkable and I highly recommend is called "Trading in the Zone" Read it please.Lots of new traders forget to train their minds about trading and get hummered hard by the markets.Technical part of trading is easy.Waiting for set up is hard for new traders and often they jump in early or after loss immediately get in another trade to get their money back and lose even more.These examples are all trading psychology related. Don't get over excited on few wins or get super depressed on losses.Keep learning from your mistakes regards and good luck As a reading project educate yourself at least basic level on Elliot Wave theory.Market rhythm often adheres to Elliot Waves.Not necessary for this system here but helps you see Price on greater context.

--- 帖子 #11746 ---
Hi P I don't understand why you are obsessed what traders post here.Lot of traders including myself pay attention to PA What does exactly mean price action?Most people overlook what constitute PA What is 'Price Action' Price action is the movement of a security's price. Price action is encompassed in technical and chart pattern analysis, which attempt to find order in the sometimes seemingly random movement of price . Swings (high and low), tests of resistance and consolidation are some examples of price action. The candlestick and price bar are important tools for analyzing price action, since they help traders visualize of price movement. Candlestick patterns such as the Harami, engulfing pattern and cross are all examples of visually interpreted price action. I use fibs,pivots as part of my technical analyses of PA.Is it part of this system? Not directly but PA is part of it . I hope that answered your inquire

--- 帖子 #11754 ---
Very interesting question and a perfect example of the problems faced in trading. In this case the answer to the failed trade likely lies with the behavior of the GBP leg of the cross, crosses are synthetic entities, their prices are derived from the majors. In this case I would expect that the pound jumped for some reason, news or rumour. I always watch the behavior of the legs of each cross for hints towards future price action. One question I have is whether or not crosses respect pivots and fibs as much as the majors due. for example if the pound is approaching the 38 level, but the GA is not, is the S/R level on the pound likely to be more effective than that of the cross? Hi Scorps Most don't know it because its not default number on most fib indicators.This number was "discovered" by Scott Carney and I only found out after reading his books. To me it makes sense from market. Big boys love taking stops so 618 fib is popular hence very likely to be zone of interest for stops and orders but pushing through little higher or lower will take care of stops and once that accomplished orders are reversed.This is why almost all swings end with a spike.One thing to keep in mind that price can also violate 78.6 and according SC most instances it will reach or pass original measurement.That's why he says its "last chance reversal" Regards

Hi V2 Allow me to chip in a little.Looks like you are a new trader.Trading is challenging and as new trader you should try minimizing your risk. One way to do is avoid trading crosses specially all G crosses in particular GN GA GJ Why is this? For one they are fast!! Typical stops of 15-20pips does not work because one small spike can reach 50pips in flash. When you start body building you start with weights that you can comfortable handle.One does not place 150LB push ups when one can only lift 50lb.Time needed to get stronger.Trading is same.Avoid crosses until you are confident what you are doing. Personally I trade 95% majors and 5% crosses.Why? Spread,volatility does not suit me.I am sure others do well but trying to give you insight GU travel average 100pips a day GN close to 300 Think which one you make a mistake will hurts you the most .Professional traders think about risk 1st.Rookies and most retail traders think profits 1st.Risk must be a priority number 1! that is capital preservation. I think I said enough rest is up to you. regards

[but the name does not mean they r not important].... the problem is u can make up just about any 'fib ratio' so back testing this is mega important ....some EWT traders say this is the deepest a wave 2 can goes before invalidation

--- 帖子 #12120 ---
Hi V I trade with multiples because Price X is seldom nailed at right moment meaning between X and Y there could be 20-30pips difference.Traditional way is to take the loss but my way I add more to it.Combine together all trades are 1 unit Trades must be in sink with TMS30 That's how I trade but don't recommend to inexperienced traders. I got 5 years sports gambling and 5 years trading experience. Stay with single trade Its about risk management.Small is good in my opinion.Think always about risk and profits will take care of themselves Big lot even single lot is substantial when power of leveraged is applied and that works both ways.You take 3 small losses 20pips each that's 600 dollars negative.Now in order to dig yourself out you must hit a winning trade bigger then 60pips and that's a psychological pressure that often new traders are not equipped yet.Ego and "I want my money back now" takes over and you start making more mistakes and what was 600 loss becomes 3k loss and the hole gets deeper. You see a pattern? that a trader who lost his/her control all because he/she was not ready to trade larger lots.Train your mind

Worth reading Australian dollar's rise could prompt RBA to step in, join global 'currency wars' The Reserve Bank of Australia might have to step in to stop the recent surge in the dollar if it continues to push higher, economists say. Key points: Dollar has climbed over 1pc this year, to over $US0.73 this week Unexpectedly strong economic data, rising commodity prices, US dollar's fall blamed RBA may cut interest rates to historic lows, economist says Analysts said a stronger Australian dollar has the potential to derail recent economic growth, which could prompt Australia's central bank to join the fight in the global "currency wars". Danger of dollar appreciating too much Head of investment strategy at AMP Shane Oliver said while there were positive factors pushing the dollar higher, there was a real danger of it appreciating too much. "My feeling is that in the short-term we could see more upside in the Aussie dollar," he said. "And that the Reserve Bank will become increasingly uncomfortable, so they'll start to come out and say: 'Well, basically, we think it should be lower.' "Then going to the extra step of actually intervening in the market, I think, would require a very strong rise in the Aussie dollar." Independent economist Saul Eslake said there was a middle-ground where the Reserve Bank could drop interest rates to new historic lows. That could have the effect of driving the currency back down to more comfortable levels for policy makers. "If the currency gets up into the high 70s, the Reserve Bank may well consider cutting interest rates again ," he said. Meanwhile, traders are doing their best to anticipate where the currency is going to go next. "The reality is that traders don't actually feel it as stress. And so for them having something that is fast-moving, fast-paced they see it as a rewarding occupation," Mr McCarthy said.

--- 帖子 #12342 ---
It depends on what sort of drawdown Davit has built into his system. Looking at your trades in your Trade Explorer, you trade with high leverage, and I wouldn't be able to trade the way Davit does either, but he is prepared for drawdown and his risk is very small on each trade, so not likely at all to blow his account trading the way he does. When you lose 6 pips you have lost around 6% of your account, whereas to lose 6% of Davits account he would probably need to be wrong by 200 pips or even more so it can't be said that the way he trades is the way to blow an account, many would say trading with the sort of leverage you do would be the way to blow an account, but what if someone said that to you, would you appreciate it or be very offended. The point is, each to his own, you are comfortable with very high leverage and scalping, Davit is comfortable with the way he trades with very very low leverage and holding because his educated guess is that its going to turn around before he has to pull the plug on it. Neither one is more likely to blow their account than the other in the right hands, its when you don't know what you're doing that will blow the account.

Below are the indicators I used on my recent trades. Please observe carefully the colored "blue"angles or I called it, Continuum Angles or for gals, they can call it the Blue Angels The continuum angles shows up on the last row of values of the TMS Angleator ( by griffinsSoul - Again, thank you for sharing this one GS ). IMO, The continuum angles provides you an idea that it maybe facing an S/R. So take a look on how it behaves to that, and then if it comes back with a much clearer PA then it will break that S/R. It depends on how strong that S/R or strong that wall is, So make it sure that check/verify if there are real S/R on that particular TFs based on what the continuum angles indicates . You may also check the TDI level values (20s, 32, 50s, 68, 80s) of that TF or see it on your chart for the possible fibs, pivots, and of course those Divs that I'm still struggling to identify compare to LK who has an eagle eye for it In short, you can make your own rules based on this continuum angles. I used the continuum angles by loading the pair I want to trade on an M30 chart first, and then I look on left &amp; right side of the TFs (M30 as the center). If I could see a viable trade entry for scalping on lower TFs or I just go on the usual way of TMS M30 strategy,, then I go for a coffee break and comeback If I can find a more viable one . Note, that you can do the same way on a slower TDI input (default settings). This would also complement your existing strategy, if not, then of course don't use it ever, why add something that works already. When loading the TMS Angleator on your chart, choose the TDI Input &gt;&gt;&gt; TDI_FAST_4 ( Not the famous movie ). The idea of using the faster TDI settings was shared by Davit recently to me, and telling us that he loves to trade smaller lots, as well as making me look the other way when facing the monster GBPNZD, he described this one a f* fast, not good for noobs like me. --- 帖子 #12578 ---
I often give advice not to trade Asian session (as there are a lot of fake moves) unless you are very good at reading PA. To give you a straight answer, from what s available to you, if you spot a signal on M30, check D1 H4 for congruence if they are green/red and same direction of your trade, you enter. It sound like you trade H4 but enter on M30 for a better price. You can pick any pair but stick with the above rule. You won't do any good if you trade M30 and only look at M30 during Asian session as the moves are small and candles have lots of long wicks/tails and you could end up in and out of your trades with losses. Give me a signal if you have one right now so I can show what to look for...you will learn faster and remember more if it comes from you.

Hello Mudosh, I wasn't in that trade because I didn't get a trendline break where you did. This is the murky area of drawing trendlines. I have much more faith in trend lines drawn from a distinctive low (or high) at or near the beginning of the trend (as in my screen shot) than I do from some point after the trend has started. I also want my trend line to line up exactly with three lows in an up trend. K Attached Image (click to enlarge) Edit: I note Lastingwell's post. I'll qualify my text above by saying that I would need a trendline break before I would even CONSIDER a short.

Hi Mudosh, I followed Phx62 on the TMS thread for years but could never replicate his excellent trades. When I came over to this thread I noticed that the 30m chart gave me enough bars to draw a trendline and that, way more often than not, good moves were preceded by a trendline break. I don't lose any sleep wondering about the mysteries of Fibonacci on trading charts and, for me, trendlines drawn EXACTLY on 3 lows in an up trend, or 3 highs in a down trend, are just the same. I have no idea why they line up exactly, but they do. The majority of my trades are taken when at least these 3 rules are met: trendline break, rejection from s/r, and close outside the PAC. I hope this gives you some food for thought. K

--- 帖子 #12953 ---
I got a few PMs asking for advice. One of those I thought it'd better to be answered in here so others might benefit as well. ---------------------------------------------- "I started reading first the original TMS thread and have gone to about 80 pages of BigEposts, At that time Mr Aussie started the TMS for newbies , i thought it will be good for me to start but again i am lost which system to follow. Also please as you are expert in TMS , i will highly appreciate if you can guide / suggest direct me from where to start so that I can learn the TMS trading and also absorb it. Please I also need you you help in some good tutorial of Support resistant and the Price action. I am based in UK and using Alpari Broker GMT+2. Been demoing using lot 0.1 since last month taken two trades wrong and still runny the loss on -250 and -150 overall account is approx plus 700. i do a day job from 08:00 to 18:00 GMT again will be grateful as what you recommend me how to trade the London session as its finished during my job hours but as Big E mentioned I can log in my MT4 and have a look on whats happening every 4 hours." --------------------------------------------- I understand your confusion about trading and specially when taking a trade and sitting with a big loss. If you are new to trading, I suggest you visit www.babypips.com to learn all the basics like S/R (price swing high/low, Fib levels, moving average,etc.), divergences, hidden divergences, candle patterns. Once you have those skills we call price actions (PA), you can combine that with TDI/ Stoc and make it your style as you have more edge on your entries for you to take trades on any time frame you choose. Another tip I normally give to new traders is having a habit to manually draw trendline on your chart to feel the market. Don't get in a trade right at Frankfurst/London Open (FO/LO) as those moves/candle I found normally are fake moves. Wait for 15-30min then enter if there is a signal. Taking trade on H4, you have to check Weekly(W1) chart and Daily (D1)chart to see if any support/resistant (s/r) nearby, such as where recent high/low swing are. Practise to draw horizontal lines on W1 and D1 then switch it to H4 so those lines should stay there to remind you not trade into them. Having a plan (we call big picture) help when you trade H4 (check W1, D1 charts) have risk/reward (loss/profit) in place. Don't just enter a trade because you see TDI green crosses red or a candle turn from red to blue/green. If you decide to trade FO/LO sessions, look for signal on M30. I enter on M30 with these confirmation: - TDI cross/bounce - APB same color with my trade - @S/R - TL (trendline) breakout or special candle patterns (can be outside bar/inside bar/pull back candle,lower high/lower lows, higher high/higher lows, etc.) ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- 帖子 #12954 ---
Zoom the chart out to see a bigger picture, find at least 3 point to join/draw a trend line. Do the same with the other line making it parallel to the first line. You might see sometimes, price goes out of the line (stop hunting from MM) then it goes back to the channel. Of course it might keep going but if S/R nearby and you wish to bag at least 30-50pips and by the look between the distant of your entry to the nearest S/R too small, you are sitting there worried...just my thoughts not only for this trade... Today (Thurs 31st) is the last day of the month. Lots of actions from Market Makers (MM) for stop hunting (big candles then pull back). Be careful and traders might consider just sitting and watching if your signals are not there. Don't force the trade. good entry , work on to improve your exit

--- 帖子 #12988 ---
[quote=likica;8847692]{quote} Did you learn a lot while in trading room then? Hope you could be generous to share...obviously I am not the inventor of the method so some secrets have not been discovered by me , only know what I know so far from what I ve learnt from those super traders in ff and my experience , I am open to learn more. I am more than willing to share, unfortunately yourself and other seniors here already have a really sound grasp of TDI. What I learned was that I was not skilled enough/fast enough to trade the NY 15 min time frame. I learned that the TDI system is not enough by itself to make you a successful trader. Dean used everything, price action,S/R, traditional patterns, was always aware of fundamental news releases. He could see and understand the market at a glance and was always quick to credit his mentors for his trading skills. One thing his mentors taught him was to always enter on a pending order so he could get the market to pay for the spread in those days the Euro spread was 3 pips or better, he would open the New order window and set the pending order based on what the tic chart was doing in that window. Very few trades ever ran away from him. Not everything he did is suitable for those of us less skilled, he would sometime "trade out of" losing position either by hedging or by doubling down when the trade turned back in his favor. Also as so many here have recommended he traded small, if memory serves he had a $32,000 account was trading one lot. Also not going for big profits. Bottom line you need the complete traders tool kit and it sure helps to have been trained in the spot market. When I get back to Canada I will look for my notes and see if I can find some more concrete and useful details.

--- 帖子 #13119 ---
From menu bar click View From view select Navigator From the Navigator Scroll to the indicator (i.e TMS_Angleator) Right click on it and select Modify That will bring up the the Mql editor On the editor click on button that says "compile" then click on the Run button (Looks like green Play button) Close mt4 and restart and it should work.

--- 帖子 #13120 ---
To compile just left click on the mq4 you want to compile, it will open up in the editor, top of the page you will see compile, do so. Should automatically add itself to the Data folder,

--- 帖子 #13121 ---
Sometimes if you don't run from the editor after compiling it gives strange results. That's why I suggested that last step I.e run (according to mql even restarting terminal should automatically compile all mq4 files but sometimes it doesn't ). Softwares can't be perfect I guess

If you read from 1st post and all of my posts, you will see most of my trades taken from divergences and hidden divergence and lots of them I named it as big divergence (BDIV), big hidden divergence (BHD) as you need to look back a few swings to find the High/Low instead of recent high/low. If you are not sure what divergence/hidden divergence are and what price actions are, take time to go to school here All the best and more.

If you are in the process of learning, It would be better to trade on Demo acct for a few months until you know your market and your tools and build your confidence, then start trading live account with micro lot...If you are trading under 3 years, don't think about making money yet. Guppies are a series of moving average which some traders use them as levels and trade away from them (Google it if you want to find out more about it). What ever indies you are curious about, put them on your chart and watch how price reacts around them. Looking at old chart is a good way to study, watching live market is like you are sitting a test, put on a trade is like you are doing a test. If you treat trading as a business, get yourself a firm knowledge and skills to manage it. By the way, quit is not in my vocabulary If you are reading my posts and follow my trading style, first thing you should notice that is I am using APBs instead of candlesticks. Levels (Fibs levels (Davit's pivots), DOL, 200MA) are very important for my decision making, always trade away from them if price has not touched them during the day or recently. Keep reading both www.babypips.com and my posts (or others if you like) By the way, I don't see any of my setups from your GU GN trade. Remember, don't buy after those big red candles and price stepping down. We are only small traders following big guys' actions. --- 帖子 #13281 ---
Anddres, You need to use the followings setting for TDI on Ninja Trader or any trading software which support SMA and RSI: the green line is a SMA(2) of a RSI(13,close). Then the red line is a SMA(7) of the green line. 1. Create RSI in a new window. Set the parameters to 13 and close, and the color to None, so that it doesn't show. 2. Drag the MA indy into the same window as the RSI. Set the values to 2, simple, close, color = Green, and most importantly, Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data 3. Drag the MA indy into the same window as the RSI. Set the values to 7, simple, close, color = Red, and once again, Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data RSI_Period = 13 RSI_Price = 0 RSI_Price_Line = 2 RSI_Price_Type = 0 Trade_Signal_Line = 7 Trade_Signal_Type = 0

By all means watch and learn from others, we all do but you have to give something of yourself to the people these forums as well as take from what they are willing to give here. Takers just wear people out So do due diligence yourself with your trades, and your posts. "Seems to be" is not enough. Why does it "seem to be"? It cannot go both ways. Is it long or short? You tell us. I&gt;E you have just posted the same chart saying it will go long. Tell us why are you thinking to go long, your reasons, is it green crossing red on TDI signaling long, any other signals, bounce of MA200, away from daily open, bounce of or crossing pivot etc etc. Take the hint

--- 帖子 #13323 ---
Lee, I don't know why I missed this post of yours. Those trades were facing S/R, and specially GJ EJ you entered very late. There is more chance for the move to go further when you enter on 1st or 2nd candle than on 7th or 8th candle as each move usually have 5 to 8 candles. Higher Low/ higher high should be considered for a buy, and lower high lower low are for the sell. If you are not sure what I am referring, pls visit www.babypips.com to study the basics. If you are building positions, you need to look at higher time frames W1 D1 H4, then zoom in M30 or even M15 to enter for a better price. There are many traders trading fx on M1 M5 but basis PA has to be abided and only go with the trend on higher time frame. When you can't find 4 reasons (like what was mentioned on my 1st post) to get in a trade, stay aside and watch. good pipping awcharts , I noticed you let the trades running longer as long as price stayed in one side of the road (under 50MA) What is a decent TDI cross Bill?

A bullish Outside bar is a bullish bar (i.e a bar with a close higher than it's open) that has a range (space between it's high and low) exceeding the range of the previous bar. Edit :- for image you can see post no 10995.

--- 帖子 #13427 ---
Lee, There a numbers of things to look for continuation signal (another name called hidden divergence), in this case bullish hidden divergence (buy): - on M30 price has higher high (HH) , Higher Low (HL), h4 has series of bull APBs, D1 has BUOB which broke up which indicated me to only go long. - dial back to our ground (M30) waiting for a set up (hidden divergence) off supports and in this case, GU was nicely bounced off BRN 1.4300 and R38 with a nice pin bar. - I would enter from a break out of that little trend line (if I was at my PC) and exit at R61 for 45pips. - If you have a good set up on M30 with H4 D1 congruent, you could bag 50-100pips. My concern here is it is reaching ATR (it could move more but might have retrace before it heads up again) - your question about 1.4350? I would ignore. I usually pay more attention to BRN such as 1.4300, 14400, ...etc. - I don't think I set the rule that APB has to cross MA for entry?...however, it did crossed and so did TDI. - One thing I normally don't like when a continuation forming after a divergence. I have a big doubt about whether the trend will continue or just a retrace as a divergence usually indicates that the trend is now changing direction. Go back to UCAD hidden divergence formed yesterday and failed after I took a short from bearish divergence, you will notice that it failed to ( after you attended school, you get what I mean by divergence and hidden divergence). If not, go back to school . This is my obvervation for you to study and take what applies to your case. Some hidden divergence (HDIV) could resume with the trend if price bounces off a very strong support and not face any resistant.

Hi there everyone As you probably know, Lastingwell (Heather), about a month ago posted to her thread ( TMS for Newbies Part 2 ) that she had some family business to take care of and that she would be back soon. Heather and I have been in email contact for many years and in a recent email she let me know that her mother had some medical issues that she was going to assist her with. Little did I know (but now it makes such perfect sense) that Heather wasn't talking about her mother, she was speaking about herself. Heather has always been very humble and never wanted to draw attention to herself, and this is one of the qualities that made her become the great and completely ego free and unselfish trader that she became. This morning I received a very sad email from her family (that I will paste below for you) to say that Heather passed away on May 2nd.. This is a big shock to me, and I feel very sad to have lost not only a great trader, but also a great friend with whom I shared many of life's tribulations not even related to trading. Heather was one of the few talented and humble people who I know first hand had 'made it' in this business. She was not 'flashy' or ego driven and in fact I know that she did some wonderful things for not only her family, but also for other traders she only ever 'met' on line. Heather was not only a great trader, she was great human being and the world will be a little darker without her. I will miss her a lot and all you and I can do is remember the simple and effective way she traded......by keeping things simple and remaining humble. RIP Heather (Lastingwell) ================================ Apologies for the intrusion but we are going through my mothers emails, we have heard her talk about you many times and we are sorry to tell you she passed away 2 weeks ago. She apparently had a kidney infection for quite a while, which went undetected until she was in a lot of pain and had to seek help. By the time she was admitted to hospital she had sepsis and was put onto life support. Sadly she was unable to fight it and passed away on 2nd May. Would you please be good enough to pass this to the forum she posted to regularly as we are sure there must be some who would want to know what has happened. So sorry to put this into your hands but we don't even know where to start. Thank you so much for any help you can give. Warm regards Heathers family. =================================

--- 帖子 #14400 ---
How do I install a Custom indicator to MT4 with Build 600+? To install a custom indicator to MT4 with BUILD 600+ Download and Install the Indicator to your desktop Right click to copy the Indicator Open MT4 Click File -&gt; Open data folder MQL4 &gt; Indicators Right click and paste the Indicator into this folder Close your MT4 and reopen it View your Navigator window and the Custom Indicators folder to see the newly installed Indicator.

--- 帖子 #14402 ---
So follow the direction : - open MT4 - go to "File" - go to "open data folder" - go to" MQL4" - Oepen "indicators" and paste your indicator -close and re-start MT4 That's it.
