--- 帖子 #14477 ---
when price bounced off a trendline or a S/R forming hidden div or a regular div and has an outside bar on M30, I would go in. I would not go in just because of an inside bar breakout. AJ in this case (m15) there was a hidden div and an outside bar prior to that entry he took and he got off the train at S/R which made the trade good. You don't have to wait for the breakout candle to complete. the critical part is level (S/R) where price bounced off and formed a hidden divergence or a regular divergence. If you took a hidden divergence forming from no manland, no guarrantee if your PT would be reached.

I think the body of the candle is too big to be considered as a PCRF candle. The candle at which you entered your short position would be a better PCRF candle for a long position in my opinion. But today GU is just in a range so I would not enter based on this PCRF setup. The best PCRF setups are when the pair is in a trend and forms a PCRF candle at a support/resistance and the pin of the PCRF has to stand out of the crowd.

Hello longbk, It's easy in hindsight but........ 1) price was creating a descending triangle where the bounces off resistance get smaller and smaller and the resistance eventually (most times) breaks. 2) Yes, you had a trend line break, but I would only enter on the break of the high of a bar that CLOSED beyond the trend line. 3) If you look at past trends you'll see that the greater part of a trend in both time and pips travelled, occurs beyond the TDI 50 line. (A 34 ema on the main chart approximates to the TDI 50 line and many traders will not go long when price is below the 34ema.) The bar on which you entered had only just gone beyond the 50 line so, for me, a new trend was not yet proven.

Kain, I don't use 10MA nor 50MA nor 200MA by themself as S/R for a reason to enter a trade. I need PA to tell if bulls or bears are strong at that moment. Of course they can be a hint on H4 or D1 that price might bounce off them at first touch. I currently have 200ema and 34ema on my m30 and trend line to watch PA reacts around them and yes, they are powerful as 1st touch. You stretched your chart too wild to see the whole pic. I need to put my m30 here for you to see if it's wise to short. I would wait for retrace to go long instead. I don't trade this pair often as it usually have small move unless it bounces off a good s/r (not the one you mentioned). From my chart, I don't count it as divergence which I highlighted in thin pink line and (which you marked). To be safe, don't try to take counter trend and compare with what I did until you have mastered trading with trend first ( you have not picked the right structure for hidden divergence either which is another name for continuation) Bottom line is, wait for retrace back to the trend line on my m30 and if there is divergence/hidden div if bulls are presented of course, you might consider go in a long. Taking note relationship between price and indicators, if price has a small move while indicator has big/long move, you will see potential for hidden divergence.

--- 帖子 #14809 ---
from http://www.bullbearandme.com/blog/ Good things about FX trading is that it is opened almost 24 hours per day with big volume in and out, while traders enter their trades from any time frames from 1 minute to 1440 minutes (Daily), not to mention trading from tick or volume or range charts. Ordinary people get confused and worried asking me that if I have a buy signal and enter and many/most traders should have the same signal and also enter the buy, who is on the other side to sell if they have a buy signal ....to balance the market and so on. Despite what I tried to explain, they seem never understood. For us as a trader, there are always 2 ways street (buy and sell) which one should we better choose to go if a TDI buy signal confirmed and next 30 minutes a short sell signal formed ? Here what is called following the trend. You would ask which trend and what time frame I am referring? I m focusing on M30, so all I talk are about what on my M30 chart and next time frame which is H1 chart while H4 is used for break out if there is an inside bar (but be careful of fake breakouts happened quite often during Asian session). I put on M30 chart 200EMA, 50EMA for direction, that is if price above those EMAs, I only think about buying if TDI and price confirmed and only if price is below and far away from both EMAs and has divergence or double bottoms, visa versa for short sell. Levels on the chart (Yesterday High/Low, Daily Open Line, Fib levels such as 50% retrace ,etc.) and how price reacts from those levels ( pin bars, doji,) are very useful for making decision both entries and exits. M30 signals 80% of time deliver profit of 30 pips to 50 pips for G's pairs while E's pairs move 20 pips to 35 pips. Your profit target (PT) can be increased if there is a confirmation on higher time frame which can be H1 or H4. What is right for stop losses (SL)? and when to move SL to break even (BE). I usually have 1:1 which is if my PT is 50 pips so is my SL ( I mentioned this in trading challenges post). I found myself exit my trades if price closed below 10EMA (if I was in a buy), or if price closed above 10EMA (if I was in a sell). Using ATR (7) x 1.5 is very helpful (considering you are not greedy:-)). I don't normally let market take me out by my SL if I am available to monitor my trades, therefore, whether I have 30 or 50 pips SL does not really say that I have to bear with such losses, but rather treat it as for emergency and avoid my trades stopped out from small retracements. Falling into choppiness is where traders get chopped out and get stressed out. I will talk more about that in my next post. Happy life happy trading to all. Lkc

--- 帖子 #14887 ---
TDI will give you the signal before the move. Usually you'll have a "correction" in price. Which means price will usually build liquidity in the opposite direction before the event. Example: Short bias will go fishing for buyers by buying and moving price up minutes or hours before the release. When the news is reported, sell off everything against the "liquidity". The herd that went long with price, and suck up all those orders. News is good timing for investment banks to either offload or load up on positions. TDI shows you this before the event. You'll get a TDI cross, Trendline break, and if you are using HA, a RED or GREEN/BLUE HA candle in that direction just before the data is released. Like with GBPJPY tonight we had a short signal just before the retail data.

--- 帖子 #14897 ---
If you trade 30M like this thread, you may want to avoid open a position till after the news. If you have open position and wasn't able to close with profit before news, you set tight stop and pray it's not hit (gambling.) If you trade higher TF such as daily, usually news won't change the direction (refer to Emmanuel's description for details.) When there are many high impact news releases during the day, it's also good idea to skip the whole day. (I didn't trade nearly for two weeks during Brexit poll.) Usually, major news releases are done by the mid NY session. I personally think it can be a good time to trade. Lastly, check Forexlive or Talking Forex and decide whether you keep or close your position after the news. To see big picture, I also recommend to read daily summary either from Kathy Lien or Jarrat Davis (free services).

--- 帖子 #14962 ---
Hello kain775, Your statement I've highlighted in red is very familiar to me. Niall Fuller's most recent lesson from his website deals with this mindset. Below is an edited version of what he said plus some of my own thinking. I hope it's helpful to you and smoothes your path to success. Most new traders believe and act as if they are going to change their lives very quickly through trading. This is folly. Your drive to change your life at the pace YOU have chosen is not congruent with the behaviour of the market. It's like thinking you can drive from A to B without using the roads – you'll end up in a ditch or a stream you can't get out of. You can only take the opportunities the market presents. The market dictates the pace, not you and your drive. Understand and accept this. You used to be frustrated when you felt you'd “done nothing” in a day i.e. you hadn't traded. Change your thinking: the focus isn't on trading, it's on applying your rules and deciding whether there is an opportunity for you. You haven't “done nothing,” you've applied your rules to assess whether it's worth risking your capital. Change your thinking or you'll stay on the ‘hamster wheel’ of repeating trading mistakes and re-funding your account. Learn from your trading mistakes and put the learning into your trading plan. Read your plan everyday. Make rules and abide by them to establish good habits. Money management: A sound trading mindset begins with proper money management. Risk an amount per trade that will not cause you pain if the trade loses. If you risk too much, you are stressed about losing and twitchy at the least negative sign rather than letting the trade play out. Work out what £ per pip you can comfortably risk. Successful traders who can take a big position size on a trade are interested in finding high-probability and obvious trade signals because they know that one or two good winners are all they need to make a lot of money. They aren’t concerned when they go a whole day without finding a trade, they're only concerned with finding good trades. This rationale holds true with a small account as well. You have to trade as if you’re already a successful trader, because that is how you become one. Change what you view as ‘successful trading’. One or two good winning trades and one loser is success compared to 30 trades where over half were losers and some of your winners were small. 3 trades rather than 30 indicates a disciplined (not impulsive and random) trading approach. Trading more accurately (i.e. less frequently) is how the pros trade , and it’s how whittling down your trading account to nothing is avoided. Proper trading is the goal and, if you do so for long enough, your account grows and you increase your position size. You won’t give your growing account back because your trading approach has been built on proper trading habits.

Keep it simple and work on your entries until you can get them right before thinking about the fancy stuff.

--- 帖子 #15291 ---
to avoid such kind of mistakes, have simple rules, be very discipline in following your own simple rules. Do Not follow other traders rules unless you have tested and share the same beliefs about the market. One simple rule which many TMS traders have since adopted in the past 5 years, is to use the 10EMA in all timeframes. watch the price action on the D1 chart witgh reference to where the 10EMA is, how far is the price from the 10EMA. the same simple rule you use on the W1 chart, is the price action close to its 10EMA, how close, is there room for take profit. Be careful when the price action is near to the BRN 00's. They attract 'PA like magnets"...(who said this?). Look at the AUDUSD chart below which I made my comments. Very clearly the price action was making Higher High, High Low... bullish trending, on the previous two days. Look at the day Open lines, they are stack above one another, with higher day close, higher previous day highs, right? Did you pay attention to the BRN 0.7700? So we look for bullish DIVERGENCE to trade the continuation of the trend of that moment. Attached Image (click to enlarge) On the chart above, there was another bullish divergence setup, can you spot that? When trading intraday, whether you trade in H1, M30 or M15. Pay attention to the Tokyo session High-Low or the Asian session High-Low, look for trades that will break away from the Tokyo session range. This way, you can only be wrong once, that is Plan A. If Plan A fails, you have a Plan B and take the opposite trade. Worst case, Plan B also fails, than Plan C trade will often run as the big winner of the day. There are exceptional days, when all three - Plan A, B and C also fails. What should you do then?

do not force yourself to see divergence when they are not really there. the market move in waves, the smaller the timeframe the smaller the waves hence you will see a lot more divergence than you will see in the higher timeframe. here is an example of what a 'good' Divergence is, there must be distinct swing high, then swing low, then swing high, ...every swing must be confirm with a TDI cross down, cross up, etc. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Back from a hiatus. Good to see you too The thing about divergence is, that it is only valid so long as it's coherent with Market Structure. --- 帖子 #15391 ---
Joe Dinapoli said about divergence: "Don't use an Oscillator to price divergence as an entry technique, unless you have an excellent means of filtering it. Even for the best of Oscillators this can, and often does, spell disaster, particularly for the new participant. Price and Oscillator divergences abound, and the market continues to stop out the divergence players. Looking back in time, you're sure to find divergences that work, but when you're going forward in time, as in real trading, the accuracy of this technique just isn't there."

--- 帖子 #15395 ---
The entire idea behind HA or APB is to smooth out price. This way you don't get distracted by every single tick. A prerequisite for this system is to have a cross on the TDI and an APB that matches. That's your entry signal. You do not frame setups upon your signal, you frame them on other means of technical analysis. Big E notes horizontal support and/or resistance, trend and swing highs and lows. I hope this helps.

When taking counter trend trades (when there wasn't any DIV with OB), I often find that 2nd set up of divergence has more chance to work out successfully ( I named it double divergence or short for DDIV), in this GA case it had 2 attempts I called double double tops TDI, I keep reminding traders to look left (both price and indicator), lots of times I drew trend lines on both price and indicator to see if there was any divergence/hidd div or double tops/double bottoms, 1st and 2nd divergence, or double div, etc. where price/indicator would turn around...there are many ways to see good setups if you spend time on your chart to read PA with indicator working together, specially if you want to be good at taking counter trend trades . It looks to me you have more attention on single candle (OB) or candles like PCRF, I am not saying it does not work but without reading a whole picture, you won't get very far. Again, just repeating that if you find a good location, any set up which can be just a TDI cross will do good pips for you.

--- 帖子 #15436 ---
Hi Kain, when you leave your house it will be 'empty space' without you being home, right? therefore when you want to trade when you are not at home to manage your trade, make sure there is 'empty space' for your trade to run into profit. also make use of the full TDI Green, Red and Yellow when you want to trade the smaller timeframes H1, M30, M15 and also M5. on M30, the TDI Green shows you the average price momentum of the last 3 candles/bars. The Red shows your the average price momentum of the last 7 candles/bars. The Yellow shows you average price momemtum of the last 34 candles/bars. Therefore if you use the full TDI when your trade M30, it will help you pick the better setups with view of the higher timeframe momentum. Think of it this way, 2 x M30 candle make one H1 candle, 8 x M30 candles make one H4. If you see many small M30 candles, it tells you the H4 candles ae also small, hence no volatility and low momentum. Next, at the time your see a setup, look to the left of your M30 chart, is there empty space of at least 10 to 20 candles distance for your trade to run into without hitting any recent buying or selling activity? Now do your own visual backtest on your M30 charts, look at only the setups when the TDI Green Red lines are above and below the TDI yellow line. Hown often do you see the setups which run into profits when there are empty space to the left i.e. with no recent buying / selling activity. I made some comments your GBPNZD trade as an example. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Next thing is when you know you will not be available to manage your trade, you can consider to use a multi-lot entry i.e. to open 2 trades with same SL but different TP. 1st trade, with smaller TP e.g 25pips 2nd trade, with final TP e.g. 50pips. This will help mitigate the overall risk when you use one single trade entry. Another way is to use a trade manager like THV CaveManager to move your SL to protect your capital and also manage multiple exits. Also important is to follow a specific trading hours in this business. Some pairs are only good to trade during the London session. For practice, look at GBPUSD M30 now, do you see 'empty space' below and above the current price action? Where is support and resistance? What about the M30 TDI? Id there potential trade opportunity? if not, then look for another pair to trade. regards,

Below is the consolidated information... Miss LK just for you. Please find the attached Beta version of TMS Angleator by GS updates: 1) Instantaneous Angular Trend Signal (Buy or Sell ) - experimental feature only - This signal can be used in conjunction with your own strategy. Thus, you need to verify if the signal is valid or use this signal at your own risk. 2) TDI Digital Clock - experimental only using the TDI clock face rule 3) Switchable Angle display - Thanks to Lukeb's version 4) Stochastic Levels - Default settings = 14,3,3, SMA | Optional settings = 8,3,3, SMA -This stoch levels are here for added confluence with your strategy using the TDI Angleator. (e.g. Mehdi's Low risks stress free TDI system, Big E's TMS-5, LK TMS-30 divs etc..) 5) New Background... thanks to cja for the help The default TDI input is TDI-RSI-10 = most commonly use type of TDI settings for TMS or TDI users. You may select TDI-RT-Clone as an option for others who used to using this type of TDI. Then, you can attached on your chart the same TDI indicator on your chart or use the one I am using ( TDI.ex4 ) The signal is looking to satisfy the following instantaneous angular trend in order of the following TF: In conditional order number &amp; groups. For now, it identifies STRONG TDI Separation value - space between Red and Green line. 1) w1_d1_h4_h1: example: if W1 separation value is STRONG then it will check if the next lower TF is having the same instantaneous angular trend (from D1 - H4 - H1) with him. 2) w1_d1_h4 3) d1_h4_h1_m30 4) d1_h4_h1 5) d1_h4 6) h4_h1_m30: example: if H4 separation value is STRONG, then it will check if the next TF is having the same instantaneous angular trend with him Then it is up to you to verify if other TF like D1 or W1 are having second thoughts in following the same angular trend or if it would do so on the next minute(s) or hour(s) based on Price Action or current Market trends. Basically, it depends on how you read the signals or whatever working strategy you have in confluence with this tool or vice-versa. 7) h4_h1 8) h1_m30_m15 9) m30_m15_m5 The idea is for higher TF trading. Meaning, it checks higher TF first, then it is up to you to decide if the signal is valid down to lower TF, but then it depends how each of us read the current market trend or what the Price Action reveals to you (us). It is also depends on you if you want to use this for Scalping type of trade entries and exits. Final version: -with Alerts - Sounds - Email for Signal -Signal settings - Moderate, Aggressive or Both Note: Please test on your demo account first as this is just a visual guide for experience TDI users. The attached indicator files needs to be inside your indicator folder and only the TDI.ex4 and TMS_Angleator_beta.ex4 needs to be loaded on your chart. The source will be uploaded once the final version is done (my code is not that efficient - not using much of an array - too amateur). If you found bugs (errors) on this tool, please reply to this thread. You may suggest additional signal behavior or something, but I cannot promise that I can do it because of my limited knowledge in MQL 4 programming. If you found this tool useful, please give thanks to GriffinsSoul for sharing his ideas and this tool to us. Many thanks and kindest regards ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- If you switch from TF to TF, you will notice the above header changes color as well. Simple guide: Green --- for overbought levels, Buy signal and TDI Arrows or angular direction (UP//Curve/Crosses) Red --- for oversold levels, and Sell signal and TDI Arrows or angular direction (Down/Curve/Crosses) Gold -- Spread color and for TDI separation (distance between Green line and Redi line) Blue --- Instantaneous Angular Trend Detection color or building up And in case, you did not read yet about the signal, please read this info from this post http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...78#post9108278 For Stochastic (14,3,2,SMA) , 76.4 is the starting point of overbought levels and 23.6 is the oversold levels. Locations are very important, and if you have divergence set up at good level, 99.99% you will have nice bag of greenies, but make sure you don't go short while TDI&gt;68, stoc&gt;75 (overbought= market too bullish ), nor go long while TDI&lt;32 (oversold = too bearish), stoc&lt;25. In addition with those conditions and with TDI cross and APB same color, it will be safer to go short when Stoc&lt;50, and long when stoc&gt;50.

--- 帖子 #15537 ---
It seems to me that you guys asking around here for L's templates have a false sense of self-entitlement. That's not going to kill you but it will give you the wrong impression that you are owed something when you are actually not. This attitude is not going to do you any good. If you took 5 minutes of your time to dissect L's template, you'd see the core indicators are : Heiken Ashi or Synergy Pro bars, the TDI which can be also recreated manually, Stochastic which is DEFAULT in MT4, ADR Indicator which is everywhere in the paperclip and the Angleator which has its own damn good thread. All else she talks about - S/R, divergence, trends, HH/HL, these are all PRICE ACTION notions which is why TMS M30 is not for absolute newbies who wait for a flash on the screen to tell them SELL or BUY. So my suggestion is go into the paperclip and search for those indicators yourselves if you want them.

--- 帖子 #15674 ---
No I did not mean you have to wait for h4 close what I wanted to say was the higher timeframe (and m30 as well) was very bearish at the time you took the trade. Look at the candle on your chart at 0.00 and the one following at 4:00 this is the defininition of an engulfing candle: Engulfing candlestick patterns takes two candlesticks to be identified. A bullish engulfing pattern is characterized by a bullish candle whose body , the open and close engulfs the previous candle’s body . Conversely, a bearish engulfing pattern is characterized by a bearish candle whose body engulfs the previous candle’s body . It is a stronger signal if it also engulfs the wicks but its not necessary. To see that pattern on h4, tdi strongly down, ll and lh on m30 all adds up to lower probability trade.

Pivots is still under my microscope... You may need to ask Dennis with regards to Pivot or even Davit, Oh! not Davit you need to be a seasoned trader, just lurk around his FF crib and see/speculate/verify but don't ask... In my opinion, Pivot will work if you don't chase it... work with it with TDI is good. In my personal observation only... the one that Davit have is a Pivot fuse with self-fulfilling prophecy of Fibonacci levels; S1 - S2 &amp; R1 - R2 respectively as 38.2 - 61.8 and extended to 78.6. He can correct me if I am mistaken here. So for now, Pivots, again in my opinion is like a prophecy.. sometimes it is correct but not exactly, and other times completely wrong. So if you become a seasoned Pivoters you'll be able to adapt or even breathe with some viable instrument to trade with it in regularity and then eventually less likely to be wrong. With Dennis, he's purely a Floor Pivoters, it takes time to become one like him. he don't chase the price with Pivots... he's very calculated. On the chart below .. I can see Pivots near those BN levels. BN levels looks a bit more accurate, why? it was made as that... a notion that those big players perceived these levels while seeing the current price movement. Below is the Pivot point formula and its corresponding S1 &amp; R1 Pivot Point = (Previous High + Previous Low + Previous Close) / 3 &lt;&lt;&lt;----- resulting values depends on your broker, you cannot simply say mine is correct and yours is wrong because it looks off by few points or maybe between 1 to 3 pips off with my chart or your chart. Resistance Level 1 = (2 * Pivot Point) - Previous Low Support Level 1 = (2 * Pivot Point) - Previous High

--- 帖子 #15846 ---
I don't think everyone did that (except those who quit) and of course not me in the early stage of when I was learning... unless you change your habit by dedicating your trading hours to trading only (concentrate 2hrs block then have a break....)...or you will end where you started with a loss (could be your money and time or could be time if you only trade demo). I don't ask you to stare at each candle forming, but be prepared for the opportunity... Let's say, you start your day by : - looking at news schedule for the day, then - open your M30/H1 chart, where you might have a few pairs up - if you see price of a pair stalled at an S/R but no set up forming yet, switch chart to higher TF to see if any S/R nearby for potential PT/SL or any conflict, - scroll chart up/down, zoom in/out, look left to see what happened recently,... - check its relatives to see how they are doing (for example: if you spotted EA @s/r, you would check EU and AU...) - if your potential trade faces 200ma or DOL or WK S/R, look left to see how price did recently...always act: "if price does this, I will do that..." It's called 'prepare yourself for the market/ opportunity) - Keep the chart that you spotted the potential in front of you, study how PA was doing in the past (of course not all history will repeat exactly but you have some ideas to base on) - when you know your chart/ your pair/ your basics well, and when the set up finally formed, you don't think, just get in. Don't wait for the door open too wide, that when time to prepare for exit... Just to share...I used to have a few whom I mentored for trading, I finally gave up because they did not respect my time and their time by doing other things while trading. If you worked for a boss, would your boss allow you to do something else not relating to work? why do you allow yourself doing it to your own business? Think about that!

Thanks to all who contributed your thoughts to the case study on EJ chart I posted. They are very good and helpful to us all who as we can see other traders' perspectives to improve... My way is not the only way to bag green pips, so there's no 100% right or wrong here. I marked all setups that appeared on that chart, I didn't say I took them all, just for the purpose of reminding you to be more selective on your entries (for any pairs) when price bounces off a strong S/R and has good structure, the set up will give you a nice bag. By study that chart, again, you then have some good ideas which one is the good set up and which one you should stay out. If you only focus on a breakout or just an outside bar without looking at location , you might end with half bag since the move not strong enough. In addition, entries are important, however, exits are more important. To make it simple, only get in/get out when price @ S/R. Patience (discipline) will be paid nicely. Phx62 talked about something very important regarding price action and trend developing, he says that in a trend , there often be 1 or 2 candles in the opposite direction of the trend , often trader thinks that the trend is reversing but in that case its just retracing pick more traders and push the trend higher 1 to 2 candles in the opposite direction dosent mean a trade in the opposite direction of the trend, make it a habit to pass on those but also you gotta learn about trend developing so that u understand when u see such pattern that you pass on that and wait for a proper setup with the trend or even a reversal setup

--- 帖子 #16150 ---
Welcome back Redxlll. Here is the info for you (big thanks to Emman): How to replicate the TDI using the standard RSI indicator. The Traders Dynamic Index aka TDI is actually 3 moving averages of the RSi data. The default parameters are: the TDI Price Line PL green line is a SMA(2) of the RSI(period 13, Close Price). Then the TDI Trade Signal Line red line is a SMA(7) of the PL green line. The TDI Market Base Line MBL yellow line is a SMA 34 period of the PL green line. You can replicate these using the platform standard RSI indicator: Steps: 1. Create RSI in a new window. Set the parameters to Period 13 and use the Close Price, and set the color to None, this will not show the RSI line. 2. Select and drag the Moving Average indicator into the sub-window as the RSI. Set the MA period to 2, Simple, Close, color = Green, and the most important last parameter is to, Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. 3. Select and drag the Moving Average indicator into the same sub-window as the RSI. Set the MA period to 7, Simple, Close, color = Red, and the most important last parameter is to, Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. 4. --- 帖子 #16201 ---
Hi Rock. Here you go. How to replicate the TDI using the standard RSI indicator. The Traders Dynamic Index aka TDI is actually 3 moving averages of the RSi data. The default parameters are: the TDI Price Line PL green line is a SMA(2) of the RSI(period 13, Close Price). Then the TDI Trade Signal Line red line is a SMA(7) of the PL green line. The TDI Market Base Line MBL yellow line is a SMA 34 period of the PL green line. You can replicate these using the platform standard RSI indicator: Steps: 1. Create RSI in a new window. Set the parameters to Period 13 and use the Close Price, and set the color to None, this will not show the RSI line. 2. Select and drag the Moving Average indicator into the sub-window as the RSI. Set the MA period to 2, Simple, Close, color = Green, and the most important last parameter is to, Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. 3. Select and drag the Moving Average indicator into the same sub-window as the RSI. Set the MA period to 7, Simple, Close, color = Red, and the most important last parameter is to, Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. 4. Select and drag the Moving Average indicator into the same sub-window as the RSI. Set the MA period to 34, Simple, Close, color = Yellow, and the most important last parameter is to, Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. Note: all three settings must be Apply to = Previous Indicator's Data. The above setup should now show the TDI replicated with these default parameters: RSI_Period = 13 RSI_Price = 0 RSI_Price_Line = 2 RSI_Price_Type = 0 Trade_Signal_Line = 7 Trade_Signal_Type = 0 Market Base Line = 34 Market Base Line Type =0

After looking at some of the setups posted here on divergence, I really think some traders don't have a good understanding of what real divergence is. It looks like traders claim to have a divergence in place when all they really have is a swing high or low and nothing else. Hint: The number of bars or candles between divergent highs or lows is very important and an important part of divergence. Having said that, if it works for you then good luck

--- 帖子 #16351 ---
My point was the reason you comparing GU and EU before trading EG works is because: GU establishes strength of G (against dollar) and EU gives strength of E (against dollar). Thus if there is a difference in the two currency pairs; then EG will be a good trade (because the currency stengths (E and G) are going in opposite directions against the dollar). So I thought can this concept be applied to other currency's... Using CAD as an example... Why don't I check UCAD to check strength of CAD. Check EU to check strength of E. And then if the currency pair's are going in the SAME direction, that means one currency is strong while the other is weak soo.... ECAD will be a potentially very good trade since the individual currency strengths (E and CAD) are going in opposite directions ECAD works slightly differently to EG. In EG you would check to see different direction between GU and EU but in ECAD I would check to see SAME direction in UCAD and EU. But the same fundamental concept is there The reason they differ is because in GU, G is the base currency but UCAD is the other way round (USD is the base currency). sorry if i'm not being clear

It depends on the currency you are pairing with. Trading those PCRF , I happen to not focus on them much anymore as they need lots of experience in the market, but when taking a proper entry with TMS often leads to PCRF so am focusing on TMS For me I dont wait for third or 2nd candle to enter a trade, I will follow proper setups based on my trading plan and then will take entry, sometimes the entry is aggressive like pin bar entries on the break above/below that bar sometimes I wait for candle changes color and only then I will take the entry so all depends on market conditions at the time , also its important to enter when market is at it best price this can help with getting ur TP hit rather than reversing just before hitting TP due to waiting for proper confirmation which sometime is already there , so best for time being is leave PCRF a side, master trading TMS and only then or in between have a look to trade those pattern until u get to know them better

The day trading method could be called "try to follow Likica/Phx62 's beautiful trades " but on H1 now. As there are not enough opportunities with 1 single currency , I added 2 others , non correlated : Cad/Jpy and Aud/NZ because they are quiet during my trading time with no news except CAD/Jpy but I stop before release (lunch time for me ) and may re-start something after news release. the other non correlated pair could have been Gbp/CHF but I dislike Gbp pairs as they are difficult to be traded according to me because of the times of release of news from England or because they are too huge movers for me ! Till now , this way of trading seems to correspong quite nicely with my personnal psychology and timing (sport , leisure , lunch time etc...) This is why I choose these currencies . Till now , I seem to be confortable with such a choice of strategies and currencies.

--- 帖子 #16573 ---
this method can be applied to any timeframe. Let's say there is a set up (DIV or a hidden DIV @ S/R) on M30 during the time I am in front of my PC, I certainly get in a trade, but if I am late and missed that signal, I will switch chart to see if I could get in on H1 or H4. If around NYO I would make it to M5 to get in a continuation of M30 signal. You get the idea...don't just stick to H4 or D1 and if you missed a signal you feel bad. Trading on higher timeframes for some traders is less stress but for others is stressful as you have to deal with larger DD unless you are building positions and that is another level on both psychology and knowledge (fundie and tech) to be discussed further...

--- 帖子 #16623 ---
I am m30 specialist as someone once called me :-) and yes, it's not that hard to read even to those who have been trading for a while, H1 is longer TF and of course has less opportunities than M30... However, my biggest tip to you and all is not about TF but having the patient to wait for a good location then look at price actions and indicators ( tdi and stoc) to get in on whatever timeframe you are trading, take what market gives you on that timeframe. A set up on a longer TF gives you more pips... I m a low tech person, so don't ask me to re-upload any more template and indies ( I don't like doing that repeat boring thing, I believe you can create your beautiful chart of your own :-) from provided indies ). DOL is from an indie from paperclip on the top right hand of this thread for your use. DOL on my chart might look slightly different from your chart depending on where your brokers are located (NY or Aust or Eur). It's vital to always look left and look up/look down for S/R nearby before getting any trade as you would not like to be hit by a brick wall .

There are 2 conditions on EJ M30 which I would not go in a long of that bullish hidden div.: - price was wandering around YL/YH unless stoc &gt;80 or TDI&gt;68 (overbought) - followed by a bearish regular div untill a bullish regular div formed. a hidden divergence is another name of a continuation of current trend. The dol is like s/r level and quite often when price reaches the dol it either bounces or goes thru ' it...if it bounces then it is acting like a s/r..if price goes thru' it easily like a hot knife on butter then it's not a strong level...just trade away from this level...When price has gone exceedingly far from the dol and pa suggests a retracement then you can trade towards it...nothing special..it's just like any s/r level..

--- 帖子 #16347 ---
there are 2 scenarios: - With the trend: it is easy when you spot a divergence then jump in - Against the trend: I normally wait for HL or LH or a trendline breakout once a divergence confirmed. If a trade goes in DD during the time I am available to monitor my trade, I usually wait to see if the price is stepping up HL HH or stepping down LH LL to take actions whether to exit or stay in. There are 3 important keys in any methodology: 1st : Locations (s/r) 2nd: price actions 3rd: indicator (s) which in our thread are stoc and TDI. I am sure almost every trader who has been trading for more than 3 years already knew these keys. However, the master key is 'self'. Some are still having issues to be consistently profitable due to only using one of those keys while omitting the other two. When we change ourselve (our thoughts and our actions), our results will change!

--- 帖子 #16355 ---
I am not an expert on the angleator but the simplistic answer is that people aren't using it because they haven't found that it contributes to their trading edge. I find that it tends to flip over too quickly, you see all green arrows and think that there is an established bullish trend and 10 minutes later half the arrows are flashing red. might be that I just don't understand all of the nuances but for me, the danger is giving me false confidence. What I do use it for is a warning of chop, if I see 3 colours scattered across all time frames then that pair is likely in chop and I am not interested in trading that pair. my 2 cents Keith

--- 帖子 #17262 ---
Hey, Likica thanks for the heads up, I am already in that trade off of the 4 hr and suffering a little drawdown, nice to see that it is likely to work out. About a month ago you gave me some advice on avoiding chasing trades, mad dog trades as I call them. Well, I followed your advice and took the time to really notice what I was doing and discovered that I was beating myself up unnecessarily. In a good market with decent swings I am a genius, unfortunately in the typical narrow range NY session, not so much and in real time I have no way of knowing if it is going to be narrow range day or not. Trading the NY session the market really teaches you to trade badly the ranges are so narrow and often the session ranges right into some of the Asian session is taken up by one news spike candle, often in the session, there are two or more candles that cover the entire day's range. so in order to get a1:1 R: R ratio, you need to jump in early or you never reach TP, and often if you do jump in early the signal turns out to be an invalid signal. So between a rock and a hard place. So I have stopped trading the 30 min chart for the NY session, just not doable for me. Moved out to the 4hr charts and that is much less stressful and gives me ample time to consider all aspects of a trade. Unfortunately, the past week has been flat and choppy, euro range for the entire week only 124 pips, AU only 74 pips, tough to get a trade in that narrrow a range. So I will persevere with patience, once again thanks for all of your hard work on this thread. Green pips to you Keith

Hey Likica I agree about trading the 4 hour, that is a desperate attempt on my part to get around narrow ranges during the NY session, I hate the 4 hr, but if NY is going to have 30+ pip session ranges I have no choice, I plan to move back to 30 minute if/ when ranges expand. I find it less stressful since my risk doesn't change just adjust my lot size, and on the 4 hour, I don't have to worry about getting stopped out by minor news spikes caused by Trump saying something stupid and the tanking USD. I do find it odd to have such large TP levels, given how hard it was to reach TP on the 30 seems even more difficult on the 4 hour. The big advantage is that the 4 hour gives me more time to enter and I am sometimes using limit orders to get better prices since on a 4 hour there are usually pullbacks. Still, my preference would be the 30, really hate holding trades overnight, and also there are a lot fewer trades per week so less opportunity to grow the account. Good, advise look left and get your mind right. One thing I am working on is not getting attached to bad outcomes, always found it really maddening to get stopped out by One pip or miss TP by one pip, now I try and just let it go. thanks again, I'll keep you and any others interested updated on my journey. cheers Keith

--- 帖子 #17312 ---
Before entering a trade, I would ask myself if the followings are met: - is current price at S/R? - where are TDI and stoc? making sure I am not going against dangerous zone (no buys @ oversold, no sells @overbought area), any divergence or hidden div? - What is price doing going up (higher highs, higher lows) or going down (lower highs lower lows)? or a trendline breakout? I would not buy EU and buy UCAD at the same time. Look at both chart and compare them yourself, if you can't read the logic by the names.

I found the most important thing in Likica's posts was waiting for a higher swing high if you want to buy, and then preferably a higher low or divergence, but the higher swing high shows buyers coming in and managed to push price higher. Likewise for a sell, you need firstly a lower swing low to show up so it shows sellers coming in. If you look at the top of your chart when price started coming down, first there was a lower swing low and then a lower high and price turned nicely. I found it far more successful waiting for that.

Firstly, we don't trade according to those rules, this is Likica's threads and you should be looking at her examples to take trades and secondly you can't grab every pip in every move, the idea is to take the trades with the strongest possibility of working and not failing. The long cross on EG trade would not have been valid for these reasons: 1. The tdi is still below 32 2. price is still making lower lows and lower highs All this had in its favour was the location and we know how often those can fail. The short cross would not have been valid for these reasons: 1. The price is still making higher highs and higher lows 2. The synergy bar was green Its not too high as it is still below 68.

There have been lots of trades this week, I watch 8 pairs, but you can't expect to just go by the alerts. The pro tdi alert especially is usually 1 bar too late I find, that's why Likica doesn't have that alert on her template. I do have the h4 tdi on my charts to get an idea of what the h4 is up to, so for instance if I think something looks good I just have to look at the m30 chart to see what h4 is up to as well. Taking trades with HH/HL's is better when you are new to trading as it is "safer". However, I take more notice of h4 than anything else along with the h4 tdi. On GA there was a doji on h4 as the last closed bar so price "could" turn. --- 帖子 #17542 ---
mr pip uses no indicators, but the thing about indicators is that they are completely useless to making a trader money without the right price action. think of an indicator as confirmation to pull the trigger, but before you go to pull the trigger the price action must be in order. I recommended mr pips thread because he goes into market structure somewhat WITHOUT the indicators. Therefore you should be focusing more on price action. When I first came to this thread virtually every trade I took was failing, I received some criticism [constructive] that I paid too much attention to indicators and not enough to price action ... i've definitely improved a considerable amount by then. There are a lot of indicators used in this method. It is much easier said than done not to become overly influenced by them whilst unwittingly neglecting price action. Personally I find the fewer the indicators, the easier it is to learn price action. unfortunately there is no easy way to learn everything [for free]. People often link to babypips school like it's the Holy grail of forex when someone asks a question ..but imo there is not nearly enough in there to become profitable ....and can be rather frustrating when you are failing left right and centre and someone just links you to the school. Also mr pip uses VIDEO'S. How long are mr pip's videos? If you typed out everything he said in one those video's [which are often describing just one trade, how much pages would that be?] now compare that to the amount typically written when someone posts a trade on forexfactory. You are typically getting 10x 20x ...even 30x plus more content on a setup from watching a video than if you were trying to learn from a forum thread where really most of the time you're getting under two or three lines. and this doesn't just go for mr Pip's video's. Most video's give a lot more content than if it were written. People are simply willing to speak more than they are willing to type. It's less effort I guess. mr pip's stuff is also taken in real time, or he plays it back bar by bar. You do not get that with forum posts. You are usually looking at trades taken after the fact, which can make it harder to see the exact conditions which actually prompted the trader to take the trade. video learning [imo] is more effective than learning off forum posts.], hands down. mr pips nsh/nsl allows you to know the trend. There are many methods people use for knowing the trend, most of them arn't that great imo. nsh/nsl quickly alerts you to trend changes or continuations. tbh you will probably have to visit many different threads/sources to see a significant improvement in your trading. There is stuff i've learnt here but also a lot i've learned elsewhere. If you can isolate the indicators from the price action you will eventually come to realise that most of the profitable traders are doing pretty much the same thing when it comes to price action, and just using different supports and resistances for entry ...and just using different triggers to get them into the trade [indicators], but the price action is the same/similar. Only over the last few mths i've come to see that. it might even be worth paying for some content [after doing your research] No one likes to splash out £££ and possibly get scammed but quite often you get video's when you pay and these are better than forum posts [imo] I paid for some stuff and whilst I am still getting a lot of loosing trades in that method, I find what i've managed to grasp there about price action has improved my tms trading a fair bit. Tbh, the stuff i paid for was just reframing some stuff i already sorta "knew" but put it in a format where i actually understood it properly and I do not know any successful EA's, sorry.

--- 帖子 #17776 ---
hi again, you seem a bit confused about divergence for the first trade price had made a new low, but the indicator hadn't. by going short here you are selling into a divergence. for the second trade you took it looks like probably had hidden divergence on your side at time of entry [by looking at your indicator] Price had not made another new low yet. Therefore you were not selling into a divergence when you went short. selling into a divergence = price making a new low, but the indicator not making a new low, and you selling on that new low ...which you did in trade one but not trade two if you are entering at low probability points like you were doing in trade one, then more times or not the trade isn't going to yield profits. no yellow market base line in your TDI either. Better to have one than to not have one imo unless you are tms expert and don't need it

--- 帖子 #17795 ---
A hidden divergence is a name for a continuation signal of a current trend. If a current trend is bearish (when price making LH LL or after a bearish regular divergence) then jumping in a bearish hidden div probably produce nice pips until an opposite div appears which is a sign of reverse (current trend will end soon). I am not here to give definitions of div and hidden div, but trying to clarify my chosen setup. (go to babypips.com if anyone is still confused about these two)

I still have hard stop losses and hard profit targets 50pips/50pips or few pips below/ above previous swings when I am not monitoring my trades. However, during NY session, when I am on my gear trading Futures, I also glance over my screen for FX every 1/2 hr since I trade from M30, more often I exited or adjusted my SL/PT if market condition changed. That is called management ;-). Why are we sitting there seeing the market condition changed and did nothing? 30pips SL /PT don't mean much to me if I saw space for more green pips or could not see any room to move??? Location is the number one important element to get my attention before even thinking about divergence or hidden divergence or HL HH LH LL, etc. If you don't get what I meant, don't worry, you will get there. For the time being, focus on your chart more and do not add any more indicators. I told you all here that I have not been actively posting here anymore since everything I shared before and now is still the same method and have worked for me. It's up to you to make it your own style and learn from your mistakes and move forward. My recent trade on Friday on GA spotting price got through 200ma, came back up forming hidden divergence (note that a bearish regular divergence formed earlier but I did not get in because price was facing DOL, 200MA ). I then added more to my current position once price got rejected from DOL again and stayed LH. PT hit around S/R for 50 greenies . I was busy so I did not check in until the party was over :-). Happy ending for Friday!

--- 帖子 #17854 ---
If going with a current trend, you don't have to wait for HH HL after a regular div form@S/R. If going against a trend, yes, you need HL HH after a reg bullish div to go long and vice versa for going short. There is another way going against a trend without a regular div that I took on GCAD spotting price bounced off support (BRN, YL, ADR), I went long after price made HL HH with a hidden divergence.

--- 帖子 #17856 ---
I don't take trade based on MAs, and yes, price usually react strongly at 1st touch of 50MA specially 200MA then it will still keep going back to the main trend, but if you have been followed my posts, I have been reminding traders to look left for S/R. If price moves far away from 200MA, and if there is a set up at S/R and there's space for your profit target, why not getting a ride back to 200MA. I still do only go long above 200ma on m5 m15 for my Futures trading and vice versa for going short in case you still wonder... Monday is the most hardest day to trade before NYO, so don't trade ;-)

If you looked left, you would wait for the price to reach a bit higher where price reacted in the past. On your chart, price kept making HH HL with big green bars and your TDI was at overbought which meant sellers were not ready yet. There was a hidden divergence for a continuation of the downtrend but You would not know if price was turning down or still making up, therefore, you would need to wait for TDI formed a regular divergence to tell you that uptrend of that swing would be changing to downtrend to continue with the main trend (downtrend)

Correctly drawn the divergence (which worked because it went up around 70 pips from the bottom. You also have the same moving average as I do on there which was also just above your buy.

--- 帖子 #18103 ---
Yes, it is a technique i learned from a quant banker that works for DeutcheBank in the United States, he used extremly wide stop losses and pyramided. But i'm practicing and i'm satisfied with the entries. And yes, they sell high and buy low. Don't mess around with useless stuff. Here, you can see clear divergences with RSI, personally i don't even have to look at RSI anymore, BB can eaisly tell you what's happening with the price, It is posibble to spot '' mental divergences'' with the BB? How? one might say. Well, see 1st wave is long and strong but the price finally declines into mid BB, And then 2nd wave also declines back to the mid BB, and finally 3rd wave declines to the lower band of BB. Usually the idea is to take the guts and sell the 2nd &amp; 3rd wave by understanding that the rally has slowed down, because there is another possibility for a breakout after 3rd wave, but one can also sell after 3rd wave is complete. This strategy was used with 1000-1500 points stop loss (placed at the pivot points exactly) And 50-700 points take profits (lower/higher band BB exits). With a win ratio of %93.7 on XAUUSD. It is an agressive scalping system and done on the 1 minute chart, 30m/1hr charts are used to pick sweet spots AKA: Previous highs and lows that price wasn't able to breach, and entries will be picked there, so 1m chart will be only traded @ those areas. An oscillator can be missleading When you are ready, ditch the RSI and only trade the BB At least that was what i were taught... And i can understand why, rather paying attention and my focus on the oscillator on a 1m chart, BB&amp;Pure price action represented by candlesticks are a lot better. Now this does not mean that I or We can perform the same as a quant bank trader,but hey it is always posib to learn. And yes they use pivot points too, lol. One more important thing i learned, always sell the green candles and always buy the red candles. TDI opposes this idea, TDI only tries to show you the '' SAFE ENTRIES '' if you will, which is also good for scalping i believe. Tekkies on this forum scored %31+ ROI in 10 days on a live account, so yeah. Anything can work

--- 帖子 #18198 ---
If you consider you are newbie, and if you completed learning price actions and this method and have a set of rules (your rules), you can trade any pairs I usually trade which I mentioned in my previous post. It only take 5 minutes to glance across those pairs to see if any familiar setup happening at the time you are available to trade, as soon as you see one, zoom your chart out for bigger picture , that way you will see if your signal sitting/facing at any S/R on higher timeframe. Another way to begin your trading day is after checking calendar for any red news, t take a tour to see which pair is sitting/facing S/R and mark it and wait for a set up which can be on any timeframe if you are day trading and if you only have a few hours to trade each day. Most newbie should stick with E's pairs since G's pairs move quite fast and furious which require discipline and more experience to handle. When there is a winner post here, study the set up, (not the pair), in fact there is always a lesson in a winning and a losing trade if we are open to learn. To have knowledge we can acquire it from a book/ a course/a person. To have experience , we need time, our effort, patience and that comes from our own doing.

--- 帖子 #18274 ---
Joe Dinapoli said about divergence: "Don't use an Oscillator to price divergence as an entry technique, unless you have an excellent means of filtering it. Even for the best of Oscillators this can, and often does, spell disaster, particularly for the new participant. Price and Oscillator divergences abound, and the market continues to stop out the divergence players. Looking back in time, you're sure to find divergences that work, but when you're going forward in time, as in real trading, the accuracy of this technique just isn't there." Trust me. Divergence is a big joke and Likica's application of divergence is broadly incorrect if not nonsense.

--- 帖子 #18356 ---
Heartening to learn that you too have struggles. I am using the approach of working on improving the process rather than focusing on the results. So instead of setting a goal of so many pips per week or such and such a winning percentage, I resolve to trade well and have specific aspects in mind; recently I have been committing to not chasing trades and not entering until the signal candle has closed. All too often I see a large bullish bar building momentum and I jump in thinking that when the bar closes it will confirm the signal and all too often in the last two minutes before the candle closes the price drops like a rock and my bullish engulfing candle is now a Gravestone Doji and my trade is well underwater. I find having a specific action to focus on and be aware of makes it easier to control that action. I also find your comment about having the exit plan very interesting; for sure I struggle when the price does not make a straight move to either TP or SL. Fear and greed are always present and become dominant when trades stall out and the original setup becomes less and less relevant. So, if I may ask, if you are halfway to TP and then looking at a 20% retrace of your potential profits do you take the profits you have and close out the position? Similarly, if you are halfway to your stop-loss, do you take a loss early or let it play out? I have tried numerous strategies, but the chaos of the markets means that all systems are wrong some of the time and right some of the time. Some days it pays to have faith and ride out the drawdown another day that drawdown will take you right down to stop loss and the 50% potential profit is gone. I do not expect to get a system that will be right all the time but would like to get a system that allows me to stay in winning trades longer. As always many thanks for your comments green pips Keith

Thanks for sharing the process of your improvement. There are many ways to trade and to manage trades and be aware of your weaknesses as well as your strengths are very important for you to make it forward. Some only focus on theirs weaknesses and do not recognize their strengths can hardly survive and visa versa. Let say you focus on your weaknesses that is entering while giant candle is forming (which happens very often around opening of a session like London and New York)... and suffer a loss so you try not to repeat it but I bet you felt bad if you did not get in that trade and it turned out well. If you don't know your strength or saying your signal's strength i.e a divergence at S/R, you won't be able to enter or stay in unless an opposing signal forming. We can always re-enter it if the signal still valid. I can give your some hintsights but can't convince you to do what you don't feel confident doing it , and only study old charts and practise on live charts build your confidence. There are reasons to enter and exit that we call trading plan. I am showing you what I did with my recent trade on NU. I entered a short with 2 reasons: Divergence and Big Divergence as marked in white and without bullish hidden divergence before that. I was not very content with my entry as the confirmed candle too big but I still got in because of the good set up. I exited it when I saw a potential bullish hidden div forming. I re entered a short at breakout of an inside bar later when I saw a bearish regular div formed on Stoc but then exited shortly after that to go to bed, and market finally reached my original profit targets without me. Sometimes I let a small position running and take profit of some before calling a day/night. I won't answer to all your questions but rather leave it to you to decide what you feel comfortable doing. I don't set my target on pips or percentage, I take what market giving me with no complain but thank you for the opportunity.

Thanks for your well-thought-out answer, essentially I start out with a 1:1.2, R:R ratio, and as the trade develops manage it from there, and as you say I am thankful for what the market gives me. I need to get better at letting trades run so I get some large winners to even out the long-term results. I am finding it really hard to live with large drawdowns in winning positions. Another facet of trading to work on. green pips to you! Keith

--- 帖子 #18383 ---
Yes, it is the implementation that is nearly impossible, have just finished a lot of back scanning, and learned a few things. I looked for some long trends in currencies and the 500 and learned that long, strong trends are very rare and nearly extinct. Impossible to tell if a 50 to 80% drawdown is just a retrace or trade-destroying reversal. Also learned that by trying to "let profits run", I was giving back too many pips. One negative was that if price action had no obvious impediments to the movement (think S/R), then I would expect the trend to continue, in reality all too often the big boys would engage in profit-taking and I would give back too much. Also noted that my trades were not that bad usually getting most of a swing and not leaving that much on the table. Also learned that in the past year I have not had any terrible trades, have been good at not moving stops, I have had terrible trading days, due to 3 or 4 losses in a row on one day. That is an issue. I have heard experts say that after two losses stop trading for the day. That is really tough for me, I tend to think that after two losses I have figured out what the market is up to. Also, I am not by nature a quitter and also many times I do turn a day around and get back to break even on the day. Essentially I am a swing trading, day trader, looking to be out of the market overnight. I started with the basic TMS and modified that and added a few of your ideas and my entries are almost entirely indies triggered and my exits are initially set to 1.2 of risk, then I will look at market structure, fib lines, BNR, I will already have looked at and evaluated S&amp;R and then I adjust the TP and SL as necessary, once that is done I never move the SL unless it is to break even, I will sometime move the TP out if the market looks strong. I always spend a lot of careful, focused time listening to what the candlesticks are telling me. I am very grateful for your generosity and hard work, so I do not post my charts, they are too far from your teachings. I will mention, somewhat cautiously, that one indie I like is the Williams %R, it helps to filter out the whipsaws in the TDI. One thing, others might find useful, I always drop down to the one-minute time frame and check to see how long the current swing has been active. For example, if I have a sell signal on the 15 and the one minute already has 30 candles going down, then I will not enter until the one minute has reset with a new sell signal of its own. This has saved me a ton of stress as often the signals generated on the 15, come just as the one minute is about to reverse. Trends within trends. I am still struggling to understand hidden divergence and will revisit that again. green pips Keith

Hello traders, Hope everyone is doing well. I received a question which was asked many times by traders," is the method still working? " What I say might not satisfy you unless you experience it yourself simply because if I said "yes" you would give me one or a few examples which failed to give you green pips and so on. Let's look at this way, if you want to know a person or a thing or a method, at least you have to spend time with them, interact, observe, read, follow, etc. A Thought for the year: Your green pips depend on your focus. What are you focusing on? Happy trading! LkC
